<type>file</type>
<content>
1: ## Context
2: 
3: - `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` (80 lines on commit `191ee9e`): prompts (lines 1-4), unused `$username` (5-10), includes `cpu`, `machine-type`, `gh-codespaces` (12-14), then `pager` and `color` (16-18), `[data]`, `[git]` with `commitMessageTemplate = "{{ promptString ... }}"` (30), `[env]`, `[update]`, `[diff]` with `diff.exclude` (51), `[edit]`, `[merge]`, empty hooks.
4: - The included templates end with `[data.cpu]`, `[data.machine]`, `[data.github]` tables, so anything placed after them without a new table header belongs to `[data.github]`.
5: - `dot_config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml.tmpl` (56 lines) is a rendered copy plus `encryption` and `[age]`; it has no template actions; `chezmoi doctor` reports it as a suspicious entry.
6: - `chezmoi dump-config` on 2026-10-30: `diff.exclude: []`, pager `less`, umask 002 (from the process).
7: - The brew hook (`dot_config/shell/rc.d/110-pkg_brew.sh:63-91`) runs `chezmoi re-add` then commits; brew-file writes the Brewfile with its own mode, so `chezmoi status` keeps a mode-only entry.
8: - Neovim lives in its own private repository, cloned at `~/.config/nvim`; its remote exists since 2026-10-30.
9:   chezmoi runs `git pull` with the entry's `pull.args` on an existing `git-repo` external target the first time (no record in `gitRepoExternalState`), then only with `-R` when `refreshPeriod` is 0.
10: - `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` is not managed (only `config.yml` is) and must stay that way.
11: - After `adopt-chezmoiroot`, all these paths are under `home/`.
12: 
13: ## Goals / Non-Goals
14: 
15: **Goals:**
16: 
17: - `chezmoi init` alone produces a complete, correct config on any machine.
18: - Every key in the template has the effect it claims.
19: - The Neovim repository location is configuration, not source.
20: 
21: **Non-Goals:**
22: 
23: - Using the computed data in templates, profiles, distro data (change `fresh-machine-bootstrap`, cem `T-012`).
24: - Removing the unused prompts or `$username` lines (cleanup in `fresh-machine-bootstrap`, which decides which data stays).
25: - Mass-applying the new modes (change `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply`).
26: - Skipping the Neovim external by profile and proving a bootstrap without GitHub access (change `fresh-machine-bootstrap`).
27: 
28: ## Decisions
29: 
30: ### Order inside the template
31: 
32: ```toml
33: {{- /* prompts and variables */ -}}
34: encryption = "age"
35: umask = 0o027
36: pager = "bat"
37: color = true
38: 
39: [age]
40:   identity = "~/.config/chezmoi/key.age"
41:   recipient = "<public recipient, unchanged>"
42: 
43: {{ includeTemplate "cpu.toml.tmpl" . }}
44: ...
45: [data]
46: ...
47: ```
48: 
49: `[age]` may come after the top-level keys or after the includes, since it is a table; the includes must follow every bare key.
50: 
51: ### umask 027 in chezmoi only
52: 
53: It applies to what chezmoi writes and to how it computes expected modes; the shell's umask (002 today) is decided in `fast-correct-shell-startup`.
54: Alternatives considered: 022 (world-readable files, Debian default), 002 with `private_` everywhere it matters; 027 chosen by the user: the user's group holds only the user, so 027 mostly removes access for other system accounts.
55: 
56: ### Regenerate, do not hand-edit, the config
57: 
58: After the template is fixed and the snapshot source file is deleted, `chezmoi init` (no `--apply`) rewrites `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`.
59: `promptStringOnce` reuses the existing `data` values, so no prompt appears when they are set.
60: A copy of the old config goes to `/tmp/opencode/chezmoi.toml.before` for the diff.
61: 
62: ### Brew hook re-applies the Brewfile
63: 
64: After `chezmoi re-add "$target"`, the hook runs `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts "$target"`, which only fixes the mode since contents are equal.
65: Alternative considered: `chmod` with a computed mode; rejected because it duplicates chezmoi's mode logic.
66: 
67: ### Neovim external, location from data
68: 
69: Three questions asked once with `promptStringOnce` and emitted as a `[data.nvim]` table after `[data]`: `host` (default `github.com`), `owner`, `repo`.
70: They live only in the local config, never in this repository.
71: The external template builds the URL from them:
72: 
73: ```toml
74: {{- $nvim := or (get . "nvim") dict -}}
75: {{- $owner := get $nvim "owner" -}}
76: {{- $repo := get $nvim "repo" -}}
77: {{- $host := or (get $nvim "host") "github.com" -}}
78: {{- $hasClone := stat (joinPath .chezmoi.destDir ".config" "nvim" ".git") -}}
79: {{- $hasLogin := stat (joinPath .chezmoi.destDir ".config" "gh" "hosts.yml") -}}
80: {{- if and $owner $repo (or $hasClone $hasLogin) }}
81: [".config/nvim"]
82:   type = "git-repo"
83:   url = {{ printf "https://%s/%s/%s.git" $host $owner $repo | quote }}
84:   refreshPeriod = "0"
85:   pull.args = ["--ff-only"]
86: {{- else if and $owner $repo }}
87: {{ warnf "nvim: no clone and no GitHub CLI login, skipping the Neovim external" }}
88: {{- end }}
89: ```
90: 
91: - `get` with a fallback instead of `.nvim.owner`, because chezmoi templates fail on missing keys.
92: - The guard is offline and cheap: `gh auth status` would make a network call on every chezmoi command, and `output` aborts the whole template on a non-zero exit.
93:   The presence of `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` only says that a login was done once; a stale login makes the clone fail at apply time, which is acceptable and visible.
94: - `.chezmoi.destDir` instead of the home directory, so the skip and clone tests can run against a scratch destination.
95: - No `clone.args`: the repository's default branch is used.
96: - `pull.args = ["--ff-only"]`: a diverged or dirty clone makes the pull fail or do nothing; it never merges, rebases or discards.
97: - HTTPS rather than SSH: the git credential helper of the GitHub CLI already serves it.
98:   Alternative considered: SSH, as chezmoi's documentation suggests for private repositories; needs a key set up before the first apply.
99: - Alternative considered: a `run_once` script that clones; rejected, the external is declarative and visible in `chezmoi managed`.
100: 
101: ### Incus feature flag
102: 
103: One boolean question, asked once: `promptBoolOnce . "features.incus" "Install and enable Incus on this machine" false`, emitted as a `[data.features]` table after `[data]`, like `[data.nvim]`.
104: The repository default `features.incus: false` (added by `add-incus-setup-hook` in `.chezmoidata/features.yaml`) applies where the config holds no value, and the config value wins when both exist (checked on 2.73.3).
105: `promptBoolOnce` returns its default when no terminal is attached, and reads an existing value without asking.
106: The prompt flags (`--promptString`, `--promptBool`) are keyed by the prompt text, not by the data path, so the checks below use `--override-data`, keyed by the data path, which the `Once` functions read as existing data.
107: 
108: ### First apply on the existing clone
109: 
110: With no record for `~/.config/nvim` in `gitRepoExternalState`, the first apply runs one `git pull --ff-only` there, and records it; later applies skip it unless `-R` is passed.
111: The step is applied once, when the user's Neovim work is merged and idle, after a read-only check that the pull would not move `HEAD`.
112: Alternative considered: seeding the state record by hand so chezmoi never touches the clone; rejected, it relies on chezmoi internals.
113: 
114: ## Risks / Trade-offs
115: 
116: - [Risk] `chezmoi init` prompts or fails in a non-interactive session. → Run it in a terminal; check first with `chezmoi --override-data '{"email":"x","gitemail":"x","firstname":"x","name":"x"}' execute-template --init < home/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`.
117: - [Risk] Deleting the snapshot source makes chezmoi think it should remove `~/.config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml`. → It does not: removed sources are only forgotten, never deleted, unless listed in `.chezmoiremove`; verify with `chezmoi apply --dry-run --verbose ~/.config/chezmoi`.
118: - [Risk] Wrong recipient breaks decryption of every encrypted file. → Copy the recipient from the working config; check with `chezmoi cat` on one encrypted target before and after.
119: - [Risk] umask 027 makes a file unreadable for a service running as another user. → None found on 2026-10-30 (the display manager reads the avatar from its own copy); `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply` reviews the full list of mode changes before applying.
120: - [Risk] The first pull in `~/.config/nvim` fails or changes `HEAD` while the user is working there. → Applied only when the user says the repository is idle; fast-forward only; `git status -sb` and `rev-parse HEAD` compared before and after.
121: - [Risk] `chezmoi apply -R` pulls into the Neovim working copy at any later time. → Fast-forward only; documented in `AGENTS.md`.
122: - [Risk] The login file becomes managed by a later change and the guard is meaningless. → `manage-gh-config` states in its proposal and spec that it stays unmanaged.
123:

33: ## Redaction
34: 
35: The public profile of the redaction tool rewrites each raw export before it enters this repository:
36: 
37: 1. secrets (API keys, tokens, age secret keys, private key blocks) become `[redacted:secret]`;
38: 2. private terms, repository names, credential variable names, token scope lines, IP addresses, e-mail addresses and non-public git hosts become `[redacted:private]`, `[redacted:repo]`, `[redacted:ip]` and similar markers;
39: 3. identity values (name, e-mail address, login name) become `[redacted:user_...]` markers, and the worktrees root becomes `[redacted:worktrees_root]`;
40: 4. home directories become `~`; `/home/linuxbrew` (Homebrew's prefix) and the placeholder `/home/user` stay.
41: 
42: The settings are in `.session-redact.toml` at the root of this repository: the public profile, the `dotfiles` terms directory of the private store, and the files that the tool's `--check` covers.
43: Run the tool from the repository root; the terms come from the private store, never from this repository.
44: The store's `dotfiles` directory sets the switch for sibling repository names to `redact`, so every sibling repository name is masked; it must not go back to `keep` until the tool keeps only public names readable.
45: Details the tool does not know are added for one export in a throwaway terms directory with mode 0700, selected with the environment variable `SESSION_REDACT_TERMS_DIR`, after reading the raw export for them.
46: Two gaps of the tool are covered the same way until it is fixed: a term right after a literal `\n` (JSON-escaped tool input) and a name next to a hyphen are not matched, so the throwaway directory holds a pattern for each term and name that allows those two contexts.
47: The tool and the store are recorded in the user's private notes; the tool is transitional.
48: 
49: Redaction only knows what it is told.
50: Before committing, run the tool's `--check` on the redacted files, run the repository's secret scan on `memory/sessions/`, and search the files for what this export is known to be about; none of these is proof on its own.
51: 
52: ## Reproduce
53: 
54: 1. Export the session to a scratch directory with mode 0700, through a file and never through a pipe (the exporter loses its tail when piped), as a full export.
55: 2. Redact each raw file into this directory, using a neutral slug for the new file name.
56: 3. Check with the tool's `--check`, scan with your own counts (store terms and sibling names including the contexts above, identity values, credential variable names, private key blocks), read samples, then commit.
57: 4. Delete the raw files.
58: 
59: These files do not follow the Markdown rules of this repository (one sentence per line, no dashes, modeline): they are verbatim transcripts.
60: Linters added later must exclude `memory/sessions/`.

 - **THEN** the outcome is `lost`, after 5 submissions, 0 Enter presses and 0 pastes
 
+
 #### Scenario: Blocked agent
 
 - **WHEN** the fake herdr answers `agent_blocked` to the submission
 - **THEN** the outcome is `blocked`, after 1 submission, with no Enter press and 0 pastes
 
+
 #### Scenario: Stall reported for an agent that took the prompt
 
 - **WHEN** the fake herdr answers `timeout` while the agent's status is `working`, or `agent_prompt_stalled` while its status is `done`
 - **THEN** the outcome is `working` and there was 1 paste
 
+
 #### Scenario: Unreadable screen
 
 - **WHEN** the fake herdr draws the screen, stalls the submission, and from then on fails `agent read`
 - **THEN** the outcome is `unreadable`, with no Enter press and no second submission
 
+
 #### Scenario: Failed idle wait is not fatal
 
 - **WHEN** the fake herdr fails the idle wait and accepts the submission
 - **THEN** the outcome is `working`
 
+
 ### Requirement: herdr calls are bounded
 
 Every herdr call of the library SHALL run under a timeout: the call's own wait plus 10 s, or 15 s for calls that do not wait.
 A call that times out SHALL count as failed with the code `timeout`.
 
+
 #### Scenario: A hung screen read
 
 - **WHEN** the fake herdr draws the screen, stalls the submission, and from then on hangs on `agent read`, with the read timeout set to 2 s by the test
 - **THEN** the outcome is `unreadable` within 10 s, after 1 paste
 
+
 ### Requirement: A workspace is built out of a worktree
 
 `workspace:open <branch|path>` SHALL find the worktree of the branch (or the given path) and the herdr workspaces open on that path, and SHALL end in one of: reuse the workspace open on the path; create a workspace with the path as its wor
 It SHALL refuse, creating nothing and naming what it found, when the branch exists with no checkout, when a workspace has the requested label with another path, when several workspaces are open on the path, or when the path is not a worktr
 It SHALL print one line holding one JSON object with `path`, `branch`, `workspace` and `action` (`reused` or `created`).
 
+

## Why

The install scripts are the reason a full `chezmoi apply` has been off limits since 2026-10-26: `05-install` would lower the system open-files limit, uninstall undeclared brew packages, compile YouCompleteMe, prompt for GitHub login and reinstall a retired extension, all because a package list changed.
Other scripts never re-run when their inputs change, or redo work on every run.
Scripts must become safe to run at any time before the supervised apply (audit findings F01, F02, F24 for scripts, F27).

## What Changes

- **BREAKING (behaviour)**: `run_onchange_before_05-install.sh.tmpl` is split into focused after-scripts, one per manager, each triggered by its own input: brew (Brewfile), mise (`config.toml`), pipx (`packages.json`), krew (`packages.yaml`), vim plugins (`vimrc`).
- No script uninstalls anything: `brew file clean` is replaced by a dry-run report of what is undeclared.
- The open-files limit comes from data, is written only when the file differs, and is never lowered.
- `gh auth login` and the gh-copilot install are dropped; YouCompleteMe is built only on request and only when missing.
- The apt prerequisites script is guarded to the Debian family, installs only missing packages, and calls sudo only then; its list moves to `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`.
- Broken trigger lines (`\{\{ ... \}\}`) become real hashes; the bat cache script also hashes its themes.
- The VSCodium script skips `.vsix` files whose extension is installed.
- Scripts share a small helper (logging, dry-run mode, sudo guard) and contain no user-specific paths.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `install-scripts`: what chezmoi's scripts may do, when they run, and how they are checked.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- `.chezmoiscripts/`: one script removed, several added or renamed; every script's content changes, so each runs once on the next apply (designed to be a no-op on a provisioned machine).
- `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`: apt list and limits data.
- New `.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh`.
- Package sets and installed software are unchanged by this change.

25: ## Goals / Non-Goals
26: 
27: **Goals:**
28: 
29: - Every script is safe to run at any time: idempotent, non-interactive, no removals, sudo only when a change is needed.
30: - Every script re-runs exactly when its declared input changes.
31: - Scripts can be exercised without side effects (dry-run mode).
32: 
33: **Non-Goals:**
34: 
35: - Changing which packages are declared or which manager owns a tool (change `rationalize-package-ownership`).
36: - Distro and profile data beyond a Debian-family guard (change `fresh-machine-bootstrap`).
37: - macOS branches: kept as they are, untested.

39: ## Decisions
40: 
41: ### New script set
42: 
43: | Script | Phase | Trigger (hashed input) | Does |
44: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
45: | `run_onchange_before_00-prerequisites.sh.tmpl` | before | `packages.linux.apt` | Debian family only; installs missing apt packages; sudo only if some are missing |
46: | `run_onchange_before_01-decrypt-private-key.sh.tmpl` | before | content | unchanged logic, `$HOME` instead of a literal path |
47: | `run_onchange_before_02-system-limits.sh.tmpl` | before | `system.limits` | writes the limits file only when it differs and never with lower values; sudo only then |
48: | `run_onchange_after_10-brew.sh.tmpl` | after | Brewfile | Homebrew and brew-file if missing; `brew file install` against the deployed `~/.config/brewfile/Brewfile`; prints `brew file clean --dry-run` output as a report; `rustup default stable` only when no default toolchain |
49: | `run_onchange_after_11-mise.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/mise/config.toml` | `mise install --yes` |
50: | `run_onchange_after_12-pipx.sh.tmpl` | after | `packages.json` | installs only venvs missing from `pipx list --short`, through a filtered copy of the spec file |
51: | `run_onchange_after_13-krew.sh.tmpl` | after | `packages.linux.krews` | installs only missing plugins (darwin `brew bundle` part kept in its own darwin branch) |
52: | `run_onchange_after_20-vscodium-extensions.sh.tmpl` | after | extension list | as today; `.vsix` skipped when its `publisher.name` is installed |
53: | `run_onchange_after_30-vim-plugins.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/vim/vimrc` | `vim -Es -u ~/.vimrc +PluginInstall +qall`; YouCompleteMe build only when `vim.ycm_build` is true and the core library is missing |
54: | `run_onchange_after_90-bat-cache.sh.tmpl` | after | `dot_config/bat/config`, `.chezmoiexternals/bat.toml.tmpl` | `bat cache --build` |
55: 
56: Hash lines use `{{ include "<path>" | sha256sum }}` or `{{ .<data> | toJson | sha256sum }}`; nothing escaped.
57: Package managers move to after-scripts so they read deployed files (Brewfile, `packages.json`, `vimrc`) instead of source paths, and so vim plugins install after Vundle (an external) and the vimrc exist.
58: 
59: ### Shared helper
60: 
61: `.chezmoitemplates/script-lib.sh`, included with `{{ template "script-lib.sh" . }}`, provides:

63: - `log` (prefixed with the script name, to stderr);
64: - `run` (executes, or prints when `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`);
65: - `as_root` (calls sudo through `run`, logs why);
66: - `have` (`command -v` wrapper);
67: - `set -euo pipefail`.
68: 
69: ### No removals
70: 
71: Uninstalling stays a deliberate human action.
72: The brew script prints what `brew file clean` would remove so drift is visible on every run that matters.
73:

78: - `vim.ycm_build: false`.
79: - `brew.prefix: /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`, the only place the Homebrew prefix is written.
80: 
81: ## Risks / Trade-offs
82: 
83: - [Risk] Every script runs once on the next apply because its content changed. → Each is a no-op on this machine by design; proved with dry-run mode and a sudo stub before the supervised apply.
84: - [Risk] Moving brew, pipx and mise to after-scripts means files that need those tools (templates calling `output "aqua"` and similar) render before the tools exist on a fresh machine. → Unchanged from today for this machine; a fresh machine is handled in `fresh-machine-bootstrap`, which may move only the brew bootstrap back to a before-script.
85: - [Risk] `pipx install-all` on a filtered file loses injected packages or Python pins. → Filter with `jq` on the `venvs` keys only, keeping each venv's full metadata.
86: - [Risk] Dropping `gh auth login` leaves a fresh machine without gh auth. → gh reads the token from the encrypted environment; the brew script logs a warning when `gh auth status` fails.
87: - [Trade-off] The dry-run variable is a local convention, not a chezmoi feature; documented in `AGENTS.md`.
88: 
89: ## Open Questions

92: - Should the brew undeclared-package report also cover mise (`mise prune --dry-run`) and pipx? (Default: brew only here; the rest in `rationalize-package-ownership`.)

## Why

The Neovim repository keeps the user's private spell words, and the terms its session export script redacts, in one directory outside every repository: `[redacted:private_store]`.

## What Changes

- Ask once (`promptStringOnce`) for the store's location: `private.host` (default `github.com`), `private.owner`, `private.repo`.
  The values are kept as a `[data.private]` table in the local chezmoi config only, never in this repository.
- Add a `git-repo` external for `.local/share/[redacted:private]` with the same shape and guard as the Neovim one:
  - `refreshPeriod = "0"` and `pull.args = ["--ff-only"]`, so an apply never pulls over local work;
  - it exists only when owner and repository are set, and when the machine already has the clone or has a GitHub CLI login file; otherwise a warning says it was skipped;
  - `private = true`, so that the clone root is 0700, if chezmoi applies that attribute to a `git-repo` target; otherwise the umask 027 of `fix-chezmoi-config-template` is the rule.
- Add `*.add.spl` to the managed global git ignore file (`~/.config/git/ignore`).
- `fresh-machine-bootstrap` task 4.3 also checks that this external is skipped without GitHub access (edited with this proposal).

## Capabilities

- `private-store`: where the private store comes from, how its location stays out of this repository, and how it is skipped and kept private.

The global mise tasks this repository deploys for any git repository: creating, removing, cleaning and listing worktrees (`scm:worktree:*`), and dispatching an agent into another repository's herdr workspace (`agent:disp

#### Scenario: Aliases resolve

## Assistant (Build · Claude Sonnet 5.5 · 53.5s)

_Thinking:_
I need to settle where the private store lives before I write anything. The store checkout is at `[redacted:private_store]`, and the Neovim tools default to that same path, overridable with `SESSION_REDACT_STORE`. The secrets tasks instead use `$XDG_DATA_HOME/[redacted:private]` by default, with `SECRET_TASKS_STORE` as the override.

I'm checking how the probes file will be parsed, with `tomllib` from the standard library, and confirming the Python version supports it. For the `secret:check` task, I'm weighing `chezmoi cat ~/.config/env` as a way to get the decrypted content in memory, piped through a subprocess so nothing lands on disk. I'm also wondering whether the task needs to respect a non-default source directory, and I'm leaning toward skipping that and just passing `--source` through.

I'm weighing how the probe table should be stored: each variable needs its name, the request method and endpoint, the auth scheme, the status that means valid, and how an expired key gets reported. Since that mapping ties variable names to providers, it stays in the private store rather than the public repo. The public task would only ever read the table, not hold it.

Settling the probe rules: a 2xx response counts as valid, a 401 or 403 counts as expired when the JSON error code matches one of the configured `expired_codes`, and other auth failures count as rejected. Network errors, timeouts, 5xx, and 429 responses are marked unreachable, and the rest of the rule set, including whether the error code is read from `error.code` or the top-level `code`, is still being pinned down.

I'm working out how the probe checks will talk to providers: the key goes in an in-process request header and never onto a command line or into logs. I also want to stop redirects, since Python's default handler would carry the Authorization header to whatever host a redirect points at, so a redirect will count as a failure instead.

I'm reading back through the design notes on the output format. The result is one line per variable with its name and status, and I'm weighing whether printing the names in the terminal is acceptable given the rule against secret variable names in committed files, since test fixtures would have to use synthetic names.

Now I'm sorting out the rule for which exported variables get listed, since the file has many lines beyond the secret ones.

I'm settling how the exit codes and missing-store cases should behave: a non-valid status for any probed key gives a nonzero exit, and I'm still deciding whether a missing table should be a configuration error or simply leave every variable as "no probe".

== add-mise-app-desktop-entries design 70-76, 97-104
The shared template and the icon symlink check, with chezmoi's `stat`, that the binary exists in the install; when it does not, the target renders empty and chezmoi removes it.
This avoids a menu item that cannot start and a dangling icon link on a machine where mise has not installed the application yet.
The cost is that a fresh machine needs a second apply after `mise install` (see Risks).


`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_30-desktop-database.sh.tmpl` embeds a hash of the rendered entries and of `mise-apps.yaml`, so it runs only when they change.
It runs `update-desktop-database ~/.local/share/applications` and `kbuildsycoca6`, each guarded by `command -v`, and touches nothing outside `$HOME`.
Both commands are idempotent.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Fresh machine: entries are skipped on the first apply because mise has not installed the application yet] → the mise install block in `05-install` is commented out today (F02); once `make-install-scripts-idempotent` runs mise before the targets, a single apply suffices; until then, document the second apply in the tasks.
- [`latest` symlink missing or stale after a manual cleanup of `installs/`] → `mise install` recreates it; the entry check in the specs (`desktop-file-validate`, `Exec` path exists) shows the problem.

== manage-gh-config proposal 1-16
## Why

Only one file of the GitHub CLI setup is under management: `~/.config/gh/config.yml`.
The rest is done by hand or by an interactive install script: the login (`gh auth login` inside `05-install`, audit finding F01), the extension list (the retired gh-copilot extension, F31) and the decision of what must never be tracked (the login state file in the same directory).
A new machine reaches a working `gh` only through manual steps, and the Neovim external planned in `fix-chezmoi-config-template` uses the presence of that login state file as its offline hint that GitHub access exists, so the file must stay unmanaged on purpose, not by omission.
Audit section 2.7 lists gh as managed, which is true of the settings only.

## What Changes

- Review `config.yml` (git protocol, editor, pager, aliases) and keep what is wanted; it stays a private file.
- Keep the login state out of the repository explicitly: an ignore entry so that a recursive `chezmoi add` of the directory cannot pick it up.
- Declare the extensions in use in chezmoi data and install them from one idempotent script step, replacing the install lines left in `05-install` by `make-install-scripts-idempotent`.
- Decide how a new machine logs in: a documented manual step, or a guarded step that runs only in a terminal and only when no login exists. No token is ever written to the repository.
- The `gh-dash` configuration stays in `manage-dev-tui-configs`; the retired gh-copilot extension and its config stay in `cleanup-dead-config`.

## Capabilities
== fresh-machine-bootstrap design 42-48

### Container test

A `podman` (or `docker`) Debian or Kali image, running the bootstrap with `--exclude=encrypted` and a non-interactive profile; success is a zero exit and an empty `chezmoi status --exclude=encrypted`.
Brew in a container is slow; the test may set `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1` for package scripts in a first stage.

## 2. The GitHub token issue
- **What happened:** on 2026-11-03, one of rog-orch's workers ran an `env | grep` whose pattern also matched `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The value went into its opencode session, so it was sent to the model provider. The stored transcript was redacted later, but the provider already had the value.
- **Where the token lives:** in your age-encrypted env file, which every interactive shell sources. So every agent, editor and tool started from a shell holds it, which is how a worker could print it.
- **Status:** the file has not changed since 2026-10-29. Unless you replaced the token some other way, the exposed token is still the live one, 9 days after the leak.
  - I can't see the token's creation date. You check it in GitHub's token settings.
  - How much this matters depends on the token's scopes and on how long the provider keeps logs.
- **Rotation, all manual:**
  1. You create a new token at GitHub, with the same scopes or fewer.
  2. I tell rog-orch first.
  3. In a terminal you run `chezmoi edit ~/.config/env`, replace the value, and apply that one target. I commit the encrypted file with a neutral message after your validation.
  4. Running agents keep the old value until restarted. rog-orch restarts its workers in its own order, and we restart our panes (me, the lead, nvim-orch, the editors).
  5. You revoke the old token last.
- **Faster option:** revoke first. That ends the exposure at once, but `gh` returns 401 in every running agent until it restarts.
- **Question for later:** does the token need to be in the shell environment at all? `gh` has its own keyring login. Keeping the token out of the environment would stop an `env` dump in any agent from leaking it. Some tools may read it from the environment for GitHub API limits, so this needs a check first.

**b. The store comment lines (private store, `dotfiles/fleet-names.txt`)**
- **What they say now:** two comment lines sit above the setting `keep`:

  - `# 'keep' publishes the names of private repositories: the owner's decision (see ROADMAP S14 redaction review).`

  - `# Every fleet repository not in that list is redacted either way (redaction tool since 2026-11-08), so 'keep' publishes no private name.`
- **Why I haven't done it:** nvim-orch's S14 session measures against a fixed store commit (`21974d1`), and any store commit would move that baseline.
- **Your decision:** wait until S14 ends, or do it now if S14 doesn't care. Either way it means one commit and a push in the private store, both with your go.

+  - isolated mode puts stubs for `sudo`, `apt-get`, `brew`, `pipx`, `mise`, `kubectl`, `codium`, `vim` and the others first on `PATH`, points `HOME` at a scratch directory and reads standard input from `/dev/null`, so a script can only call stubs that log their arguments;
+  - live read-only mode lets an allow-list of read-only queries reach the real tools and refuses and logs everything else, with `sudo` always a logging stub;
+  - a script passes when it exits 0 and both logs are empty.
+- Scripts look for their tools in the directories of `tools.search` (`home/.chezmoidata/tools.yaml`); to add directories or replace the list on one machine, set `extra` or `override` in the local config under `[data.tools.search]`, never in the data file.

+- `vim` is declared in the Brewfile, because the vim plugin script runs it and it was installed only as a dependency of another package.
+- `set nocompatible` moves to the first line of the vimrc, so that `vim -Es` can install the Vundle plugins.
+- `tools.search` makes the directories where the scripts look for tools configurable: a new data file, a pass-through in the config template so that `chezmoi init` keeps the local values, and a delta spec on `chezmoi-config`.
+- The mise script runs `mise reshim` after its install, as the cleanup of the shims of removed tools.
+
+Actions on this machine, each done with the user's explicit go and nothing else:
+
+- The mise config, the Brewfile and the vimrc were deployed, each as a single target with `--exclude=scripts`, and so was `packages.json`.
+- `mise install jq` installed `jq` 1.8.2.
+- No brew package was installed or removed, so the brew hook has committed nothing.

That is the scenario rog-orch described, and it now works: a new interactive shell started from a parent that holds the revoked value has the variable unset, `mise` uses the keyring, and `gh` reports no invalid-token message. The mise file is back to the committed content.

## Two commits ready for "commit"
1. **`fix(shell:env): drop an inherited GitHub token before the env file`** (63 characters).
   - It adds an `unset` line to `home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/010-env_user.sh`, with a comment explaining why.
   - It is deployed as a single target.
2. **`docs(chezmoi:docs): add the secret and zsh pitfalls to AGENTS.md`** (66 characters).
   - It records four zsh pitfalls, each verified here:
     - MULTIOS sends stdout into a pipe on `2>&1 >/dev/null |`;
     - two `<` redirections concatenate;
     - an unmatched glob aborts the command;
     - a variable holding a command is not split.
   - It also says to compare secrets by hash and never print a masked form, and to check the parents of a process after removing a secret.

## The facts rog-orch gave, which I verified
- **Inheritance is real.** The ancestor chain of my own pane (my shell, two `herdr` processes, the outer shell, `kitty`) all still hold the variable, as do the herdr server and kitty. A new pane is a child of the herdr server, so it gets the server's copy.
- **`gh auth token` hands out the inherited value** when the variable is set. So mise, which asks `gh`, gets the revoked token. Anonymous access was the expected fallback, and this case defeats it.
- **The unset line is the right fix**, for both zsh and bash, and the env file is still sourced afterwards. If a fine-grained token is put back in the file later, the file value wins.
- **My mistake:** I first tried to also change `github.credential_command` to `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh auth token`.
  - Mise reads the variable before the credential command, so that change did nothing and I reverted it. My earlier test of the setting ran with the variable already unset, which is why it looked fine.
  - The unset line makes that setting work, and the shipped value stays `gh auth token`.

## Not fixed by this, as rog-orch said
- **Still holding the value:** the herdr server, kitty, the other orchestrators and your editors. `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` works there.
- **Only a restart of herdr and kitty clears it,** and that closes every pane of every orchestrator. That is your call and I won't suggest it before the other work is done.

## Replies to rog-orch's other points
- **§3 guard:** I agree with the plan. For the env-dump forms to block, I have two to add beyond the ones it listed:
  - `chezmoi data` and `chezmoi dump-config` without a filter, because they print the config and the live values;
  - `mise token github --unmask`, and `gh auth token` or `gh auth status --show-token`.
- **§4 wrapper:**
  - Agreed as a change of its own. Its first task is the list of what reads each variable, which I take after the revoke settles.
  - It would also have to cover the `kitty`, `herdr` and shell startup paths. I haven't designed that yet.
- **§5 `oap/` in the private store:** I agree, with a few conventions:
  - the directory is versioned, one file per script;
  - commits follow the store's existing messages (`chore: ...`);
  - no machine-specific path inside a script, only a variable that the caller sets;
  - the README of the store lists the scripts with one line each;
  - I'll write nothing to the store without your word, since it is the store's owner who commits there.
  I'll answer rog-orch with this once you validate it.
- **§6 pitfall:** noted. It went into `AGENTS.md`, checked here with synthetic strings, and I printed no secret.

# T-068: `.state/`, the git-ignored home of orchestration state (interim layout)

## Goal

Give the state of an orchestration session (briefs sent to workers, an append-only journal, evidence, scratch) a home that is inside the checkout, survives a reboot, is readable without a permission p
Today that state goes to `/tmp/opencode/`, which is volatile, outside every session's directory and unnamed.
This micro-task adopts the layout as an experiment, one `.gitignore` line plus the first journal, and records the reasoning so that the task which norms it (`T-069`) and the sibling repos that will po

## Context digest (self-sufficient: no prior session context required)

- **Origin.**
  The repo orchestrator `[redacted:private]-orch` (opencode session `ses_e633b719cffeUqI3augjsl6tpc`, herdr pane `w9:pC`) was asked on 2026-11-07 to run each darse task in its own worktree under `[redacted:worktrees_root]/`, t
  - `~/.config/nvim`: a coordinator `nvim-orch`, briefs kept in OpenSpec change directories, a telemetry file under `~/.local/state/orchestration/`.
  - `opencode-readonly-guard`: a coordinator `rog-orch`, which during that session was moving its scratch from `/tmp/opencode/rog/` to `<repo>/.state/<agent>/` (`briefs/`, `bin/`, `evidence/`, 
- **The user's directions** (2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08, in the plan phase of that session):
  - Briefs and orchestration state need a lasting home, and `.state/` is where `rog-orch` is experimenting.
  - It may later belong to the planned per-task directories (`[redacted:private]:B-128`, the OpenSpec change-directory pattern): the repo orchestrator keeps the root `.state/` of the main checkout to steer the crew
  - Done as a micro-task so that a lasting record of this work exists.
- **Why the ignore rule is a `.gitignore` line, not `.git/info/exclude`.**
  `markdownlint-cli2`'s `gitignore: true` (`.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`, `T-057`) reads `.gitignore` files only, never `.git/info/exclude` nor `core.excludesFile` (measured at `T-057`).
  A `.state/` excluded only through `.git/info/exclude` would be linted by `lint:md` as soon as it holds a brief, and `validate` would fail.
  An unanchored `.state/` pattern matches at any depth, so one line covers the root and a future `project/tasks/<task>/.state/`.
  `lint:secrets` (`hk check --all`) scans the files git lists, so ignored files are not scanned; a brief or journal must therefore never hold a secret, and `T-063`'s rule on session exports does not r
- **Permission boundary (why the location matters).**
  opencode asks before reading or writing outside the session's directory; the global configuration allows only `~/.config/opencode/get-shit-done/*` as an external directory.

# T-065: signal from dotfiles, hook output hidden by `rtk` on passing commits, hk config hooks ignored by git older than 2.54

## Goal

Receive two findings from the `dotfiles` repository (`github.com/silopolis/dotfiles`, public) that concern darse's hook guidance and its template, and decide what darse records or changes:

1. **Visibility** (`rtk`): agent sessions on the user's machines run shell commands through the `rtk` output filter, which rewrites `git commit` into `rtk git commit`. A commit that passes prints only `ok <short sha>`, so the hook's step results are invisible;
2. **Enforcement** (git version): `hk install` on git 2.54 or newer writes config-based hooks (`hook.<name>.command` in the repository's git config), which git older than 2.54 does not read. On a machine with two git binaries (user machine: brew git 2.55, syst

This record is a signal: darse is sole judge of what, if anything, it changes (`DR-016`).

  "content": "# Signal from dotfiles to darse: shell habits that fail in zsh, and secret handling in agent shells\n\nFrom: chezmoi-orch (orchestrator of the `dotfiles` repository, `github.com/silopolis/dotfiles`, public), 2026-11-15.\nDispatch origin: `dotfiles:AGENTS.md`, sections Safety rules and Conventions (commit `b2b46a7` on `main`).\nThis is a signal, not an order: darse is sole judge of what, if anything, it records or changes (`DR-016`).\nIt holds no secret value; the point here is the habit, which every repository of the fleet shares.\n\n## The five habits (zsh against bash)\n\n| Habit | zsh | bash | Safe form in both |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `cmd 2>&1 >/dev/null \\| next` to keep only standard error | standard output also goes to the pipe (the `MULTIOS` option) | standard output is discarded | `cmd 2>/dev/null \\| next` to discard standard error, or `cmd 2>&1 >/dev/null` followed by a file, never into a pipe |\n| two input redirections, `cat < a < b` | both files are read, one after the other | only the last file is read | one redirection, or `cat a b` |\n| a glob that matches nothing | the whole command aborts with `no matches found` | the pattern is passed as it is | quote the pattern, or in zsh add the `(N)` qualifier |\n| a variable that holds a command with arguments, `c=\"echo hi\"; $c` | the value is not split: `command not found` | the value is split into words | an array, `c=(echo hi); \"${c[@]}\"`; in zsh alone, `${=c}` |\n| a bare `echo ==` | `= not found` (equals expansion) | prints `==` | quote it, `echo \"==\"` |\n\nChecks, with synthetic strings only: `zsh -c 'f() { echo OUT; echo ERR >&2; }; f 2>&1 >/dev/null | cat'` prints both lines, the `2>/dev/null` form prints `OUT` only; `printf 'AAA\\n' > a; printf 'BBB\\n' > b; zsh -c 'cat < a < b'` prints both, `bash -c` prints `BBB`.\n\n## Secret handling in an agent shell (three rules, same record)\n\n1. Compare secrets by hash in memory, never by value, and never print a masked form: a masked display keeps its last characters (a token display of `mise token` ends with the last four).\n2. Removing a secret from the file that sets it does not remove it from processes that inherited it.\n   A terminal or multiplexer started before the removal still holds the variable, and every new shell under it inherits that copy, so tools that prefer the variable over a stored login keep using the revoked value.\n   Check the parents of a process with a count only (`grep -c` on `/proc/<pid>/environ`), and unset the variable in the shell startup file before the file that sets it is read.\n3. A tool that is read-only on paper can still print a secret (a `credential_command`, a `token` subcommand, an environment dump): unfiltered listings of `env`, `printenv`, `chezmoi data` or `gh auth token` belong in the same class as reading the secret file.\n\n## Where it could land (darse decides; none of this is a design)\n\n- `template/AGENTS.md.jinja` (1.5 KB) has no section on shell habits or secret handling in agent sessions; a short block there reaches every repository generated from the template.\n- The agentic and secrets modules planned in `M-009`, and `DR-025` (secret scanning and redaction), are the nearest records; rules 1 to 3 are about what a session prints, which `DR-025` covers for files and exports and not for command output.\n- A check is possible but not asked for: a lint on briefs and scripts that flags `2>&1 >/dev/null |` would catch the habit that leaked the credential.\n\n## Return signal\n\n[redacted:private]'s orchestrator reads this file and answers once, by `herdr agent prompt chezmoi-orch \"<one line>\"` (when `herdr agent get chezmoi-orch` fails, prompt the pane of the tab labelled `orch` in the herdr workspace of the `dotfiles` repository, found with `herdr tab list` and `herdr agent list`), with either the id of the darse record that takes it or a refusal with its reason.\nThe dotfiles orchestrator reads back that record's `status` at the next re-import (`DR-009`); no deadline, nothing is pushed in darse by the sender.\n"

## Goal (decided by the maintainer: option "launcher", hybrid with the GitHub line already gone)
The maintainer's own opencode sessions, and every agent started from his shells, start WITHOUT secret-named variables in the process environment, because opencode, its tools and its plugins do not need them and
every agent can print them (and what it prints is stored and sent to the model provider). My fleet's workers already get this from launch-worker.sh (it unsets them in the pane before the agent starts and refuses to send the
brief if the agent's process still holds one, by count). This change protects everything else.

## Step 1: the list of readers, before any code
For each of the ten remaining secret-named variables of the env file (names, as you know them; the GitHub one is gone): what reads it? Skills, scripts, services, editor plugins, MCP servers, shell functions. For each reader: does it
run INSIDE an agent session (it would break there) or only in the maintainer's own shell? Only names and reader names in your answer, never a value. Facts I checked: opencode itself needs none (its providers are in auth.json; the global
config has no MCP servers and no {env:} references); gh and git use the keyring login; mise uses `gh auth token`.

## Step 2: the wrapper (a change of its own, proposed to the maintainer by you)
Shape I suggest, adjust freely: an `opencode` shell function (herdr starts agents by typing the command in an interactive shell, so a function applies to herdr-started agents too) or a wrapper earlier in PATH, that runs the real opencode
with `env -u NAME` for every exported variable whose NAME matches this pattern, minus a keep-list from step 1:
  TOKEN | SECRET | PASSWORD | PASSWD | API_?KEY | ACCESS_?KEY | PRIVATE_?KEY | CREDENTIAL      (uppercase names; sockets and paths such as SSH_AUTH_SOCK, XAUTHORITY, [redacted:envvar], [redacted:envvar] are NOT in scope)
The wrapper must compute the names at run time from the environment (not a hard-coded list), so a new variable is covered without editing it. It passes arguments through unchanged (opencode -s, run, serve...).
For readers that must keep working inside agents (if any): give THEM the key by their own means (a credential helper, their own config file with mode 0600), not through the environment; list those cases in step 1 and decide per case with the maintainer.

## Verification (count only, never print names or values)
- In a session started through the wrapper: the count of entries matching the pattern in /proc/<opencode pid>/environ is 0 (the pid comes from `herdr pane process-info --pane <id>`; the check is `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/PID/environ | cut -d= -f1 | grep -Ec 'PATTERN'`).
- A reader from step 1 that is meant to keep working is tested in its own context.
- opencode starts, resolves its provider from auth.json, and a plan agent shows its rules.

## Not in scope
Restarting herdr, kitty or the other orchestrators (the maintainer's call), the plugin's redaction (a safety net that comes later in this repository), per-command credential injection (rejected: it would make a plugin a credential broker).

## The finding that changes step 2
The secrets are in the whole desktop session, not only in shells:
1. The login profile loads the shell rc files, which export the secrets.
2. `/etc/X11/Xsession.d/95dbus_update-activation-env` imports that environment into systemd's user manager. I confirmed it holds all ten names, the revoked `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `CURRENT_SHELL`, which only the profile sets.
3. kitty is started by systemd, and herdr by a shell under kitty. So every process of the session holds them, including browsers and editors started from the desktop.

Two consequences:
- **A wrapper for opencode protects agents and their children, but nothing else.**
- **Restarting herdr and kitty won't clear the revoked `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** If you start them from the desktop, systemd injects it again until you log out and back in, or run `systemctl --user unset-environment`. I haven't run that.

## Decisions for you
1. **Scope of the launcher change** (an OpenSpec change of its own):
   - **Wrapper only.** A shell function `opencode` strips every name matching the pattern at run time and passes arguments through. This is the narrow fix rog-orch asked for.
   - **Wrapper plus no export in login shells (my recommendation).** The second part stops the desktop session and systemd's user manager from holding the secrets. Your interactive shells still source the file, so `mods`, `llm` and nvim keep working.
   - **Per-tool key files.** Give each CLI its own 0600 config instead of the environment. This is larger and can come later.
2. **Keep-list:** may an agent run `datalab`, `mods`, `llm` or `sgpt`? If yes, they get a key file of their own.
3. **`systemctl --user unset-environment` now** for the eleven names? It is runtime only and clears nothing on disk. It does not help the existing kitty and herdr, but new desktop launches would stop inheriting them.

## One more flag
The cem migration checklist, item 4.4, names `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `[redacted:envvar]` and `[redacted:envvar]` in a repository that will become public. Item 4.4 is obsolete now that the token line is gone.   "content": "## Why\n\nEvery agent started from the user's shells inherits every secret-named variable of the private environment file, and an agent can print its environment: in November 2026 one did, and what it printed was stored in its transcript and sent to the model provider.\nopencode, its tools and its plugins do not need those variables: its providers come from its own login file (mode 0600), and `gh`, `git` and `mise` use the keyring login of `gh`.\nThe agents of the fleet's own runs already start without them; the agents the user starts by hand, and the ones herdr starts in his shells, do not.\nSource: request of the orchestrator of the opencode-readonly-guard repository, 2026-11-15, decided by the user on 2026-11-16 as the first part of the launcher change (the second part, no export in login shells, is a backlog study); credential handling is audit section 2.1 and F10, F11, F12.\n\n## What Changes\n\n- **A shell function `opencode`** in the shared shell startup (`home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`), defined for bash and zsh interactive shells, that runs the real `opencode` with `env -u NAME` for every exported variable whose name matches an uppercase pattern: `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `[redacted:envvar]` (with or without the underscore), `[redacted:envvar]`, `[redacted:envvar]` and `CREDENTIAL`.\n  - The names are computed from the environment at each call, so a variable added later is covered with no edit; the keep-list is empty, because the inventory found no reader inside an agent session.\n  - Arguments and the exit status pass through unchanged (`opencode -s <id>`, `run`, `serve`, `attach`).\n  - Sockets and paths such as the ssh agent socket, the display authority file and the terminal's public key are not matched.\n  - The parent shell keeps its variables, so the clients the user runs himself keep working.\n- **A bypass that is explicit**: `command opencode` runs the real binary with the full environment, and is documented as such.\n- **Tests** in a scratch directory with synthetic variables, in zsh and in bash, and a live check on a herdr-started agent (count of matching names in the agent process, never the names or values).\n- **`AGENTS.md`** gets one line in the Commands section: agents started from a shell run through this function.\n\n## Capabilities\n\n### New Capabilities\n\n- `agent-environment`: which variables an agent started from the user's shells may inherit, how the wrapper decides, what it leaves alone, and how that is checked without printing a name or a value.\n\n### Modified Capabilities\n\nNone.\n\n## Impact\n\n- New file `home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`, sourced by `shellrc` like every file of that directory; no data, no template, no script.\n- Shell startup gains one function definition and no command: it is not run at startup, only when `opencode` is called.\n- Not covered, on purpose: processes that do not go through an interactive shell of the user (a launcher of the desktop, cron, an ssh command, a script that calls the binary by path), other agents (`codex`, `pi`, `goose`), and the processes of the desktop session that already hold the variables.\n  Those are the backlog study of secrets held by the desktop session, and the question of agents running key-reading clients, which depends on the agent-harness decision and is out of this change.\n- Applying it is a single-target deployment (`chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts ~/.config/shell/rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`) and takes effect in new shells only.\n\n<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->\n"

{
  "filePath": "~/.local/share/chezmoi/openspec/changes/add-agent-env-wrapper/design.md",
  "content": "## Context\n\n- The private environment file is sourced by `home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/010-env_user.sh` in every interactive shell; `shellrc` then sources every `rc.d/*.sh` in name order, in bash and in zsh.\n- herdr starts an agent by typing the bare command (`opencode`) into an interactive shell of the pane; checked on 2026-11-16 with a marker function standing in for the agent: the function ran, so a shell function applies to herdr-started agents.\n  The same holds for a command typed by hand.\n- Where `opencode` resolves today: mise's own install directory (mise's activation puts it ahead of the shims); a function wins over both, whatever the `PATH` order.\n- Inventory of 2026-11-15 (start evidence for the study in the backlog): the environment file holds 10 assignments, all uppercase, all matching the pattern below; nothing in a skill, task, script, config or MCP server reads them inside an agent session; opencode keeps its providers in its own login file (mode 0600).\n- Checked on 2026-11-16 with the real binary: with every matching name removed from its environment, `opencode --version` prints its version, `opencode models anthropic` lists models and `opencode auth list` shows its three stored providers; a child of the stripped command holds 0 matching names in `/proc/<pid>/environ`.\n- The secrets also sit in the systemd user manager and in the terminal and multiplexer processes (import of the login environment by the display manager's startup): a wrapper does not touch them.\n\n## Goals / Non-Goals\n\n**Goals:**\n\n- Agents started from the user's interactive shells, and their children, hold none of the secret-named variables.\n- A variable added to the environment file tomorrow is covered with no edit.\n- Nothing the user runs himself in the shell changes.\n\n**Non-Goals:**\n\n- Stopping the export of the secrets in login shells, or cleaning the systemd user manager (backlog study: secrets held by the desktop session).\n- Whether an agent may run key-reading command-line clients, and giving them keys by other means (backlog item, depends on the agent-harness decision); until it is studied those clients are not allowed in agent sessions.\n- Other agents (`codex`, `pi`, `goose`): the same function can be generalised later; nothing is built for them now.\n- A plugin or a guard that redacts output (a safety net that comes in the guard's own repository).\n\n## Decisions\n\n### A shell function, in its own rc.d file\n\n```sh\n# 445-tools_opencode.sh: start opencode without the secret-named variables of the shell\nopencode() {\n  command env $(env | sed -n 's/^\\([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\\)=.*/\\1/p' \\\n    | grep -E '(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|API_?KEY|ACCESS_?KEY|PRIVATE_?KEY|CREDENTIAL)' \\\n    | sed 's/^/-u /') opencode \"$@\"\n}\n```\n\n- `command env ... opencode` makes `env` look the binary up on `PATH`, so the function does not call itself.\n- The command substitution is split into words by both shells (zsh splits the result of `$(...)`, though not a plain variable), and the names hold only letters, digits and underscores, so no glob or quote can appear.\n- Names are read from `env` output at each call: the environment of the call, not a list written in a file.\n- Alternatives considered:\n  - a wrapper script earlier in `PATH`: mise's activation reorders `PATH` in every shell, so the order is not stable; a function does not depend on it;\n  - a hard-coded list of the ten names: it would name secret variables in a public repository, and miss the eleventh;\n  - setting the function from a mise task or an alias: an alias cannot hold the loop, a task is not run when herdr types the command.\n\n### Pattern\n\nUppercase names containing `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `[redacted:envvar]` or `APIKEY`, `[redacted:envvar]` or `ACCESSKEY`, `[redacted:envvar]` or `PRIVATEKEY`, `CREDENTIAL`.\nChecked against the current environment (143 names in the user manager, the interactive shell's own): it matches the ten variables of the environment file and the revoked GitHub variable, and nothing else; `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `XAUTHORITY`, `[redacted:envvar]` and `[redacted:envvar]` are not matched (they hold paths, sockets or public values).\nLowercase and mixed-case names are not matched: none exists today, and a lowercase secret would be a different convention to decide (noted as a limit, below).\n\n### Keep-list: none, and no switch\n\nThe inventory found no reader inside an agent session.\nThere is no environment variable or flag that turns the stripping off, because a switch an agent can set from its own shell would defeat it; the explicit bypass is `command opencode`, typed by the user.\n\n### Where the file sits\n\n`rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`, in the tools block, after mise's activation (415), because it documents the reason and the tools block is where the shell's tool setup lives.\nThe order does not matter for correctness: the function runs `opencode` at call time.\n\n### Checks without printing a name or a value\n\nThe counts use `tr '\\0' '\\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | cut -d= -f1 | grep -Ec <pattern>`, with the pid of the agent process from `herdr pane process-info`, never the names.\n\n## Risks / Trade-offs\n\n- [Risk] The function covers only shells that source the rc.d files. → Documented in the proposal (impact): cron, ssh commands, desktop launchers and scripts that call the binary by path are not covered; the study in the backlog decides what else.\n- [Risk] A script or an agent runs `command opencode` or the binary by path and bypasses the function. → The wrapper protects against the default path, not against a hostile agent; the guard and the study are the next layers.\n- [Risk] A multi-line value that holds a line shaped like an assignment adds one extra `-u` for a name that is not set. → `env -u` of an unset name is a no-op; seen in the tests and harmless.\n- [Risk] `env` is slow on a huge environment. → 143 names today; the cost is measured in the tasks and expected in the milliseconds, paid once per agent start.\n- [Limit] Lowercase and mixed-case secret names are not covered. → None exists on this machine; the check in the tasks fails loudly if one appears (it counts names that match case-insensitively and are not matched by the pattern).\n- [Limit] The kitty and herdr processes, and the systemd user manager, keep the variables until a re-login or reboot, and a restart of them from the desktop re-imports them. → Not in this change; the backlog study owns it, and the check after the next reboot is a backlog item.\n- [Trade-off] A function in the user's startup files shadows `opencode` for every call in that shell, including `opencode --version`; the cost is one `env` call.\n\n## Open Questions\n\n- Should the same function cover `codex`, `pi` and `goose` once the agent-harness decision is taken? Default: no, one function per agent when it is decided.\n\n<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->\n"
}

## The change `add-agent-env-wrapper` (audit row 27, no dependency)
A shell function `opencode` in `home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`:
- **Behavior:** it runs the real binary with `env -u` for every uppercase exported name matching rog-orch's pattern, computed at each call. The keep-list is empty, there is no switch, and the bypass is typing `command opencode`. Arguments and status pass through.
- **What I measured while designing it:**
  - **Stripping:** zsh and bash both leave 0 matching names in the child's `/proc/<pid>/environ`. With 20 matching names set, only the multi-line value's embedded line remained, and removing that value gave 0.
  - **opencode:** the real binary starts with every matching name stripped, and `opencode auth list` shows its three stored providers.
  - **herdr:** `herdr agent start` types the bare `opencode` into the pane shell, so the function is called. I tested it with a marker function in a scratch tab and closed the tab by id; your four tabs are intact.
  - **Cost:** the name computation takes about 6 ms.
  - **Missing binary:** the message comes from `env` (status 127), not from the shell. I corrected the spec to say so.
- **Not covered, and written down:**
  - cron, ssh commands and desktop launchers;
  - other agents (`codex`, `pi`, `goose`);
  - lowercase secret names (none exist here, and a task fails if one appears);
  - everything the desktop session already holds.
- **Public rules:** I generalised a sibling-repository name I had written in the proposal before checking it against the rule. The text now names no real secret variable and no sibling outside the allowed list.

### Requirement: Public writing

Every committed file SHALL be safe to publish: no secret values, no names of secret variables, no token scopes, no private hosts or IP addresses, no employer or client details.

#### Scenario: Documentation pattern check

- **WHEN** the documentation and spec files are searched for private IP ranges, email addresses other than the public author address, and token-like strings
- **THEN** nothing is found

--- proposal sample
## Why

Every agent started from the user's shells inherits every secret-named variable of the private environment file, and an agent can print its environment: in November 2026 one did, and what it printed was stored in its transcript and sent to the model provider.
opencode, its tools and its plugins do not need those variables: its providers come from its own login file (mode 0600), and `gh`, `git` and `mise` use the keyring login of `gh`.
The agents of the fleet's own runs already start without them; the agents the user starts by hand, and the ones herdr starts in his shells, do not.
Source: request of the orchestrator of a fleet repository, 2026-11-15, decided by the user on 2026-11-16 as the first part of the launcher change (the second part, no export in login shells, is a backlog study); credential handling is audit section 2.1 and F10, F11, F12.

## What Changes

- **A shell function `opencode`** in the shared shell startup (`home/dot_config/shell/rc.d/445-tools_opencode.sh`), defined for bash and zsh interactive shells, that runs the real `opencode` with `env -u NAME` for every exported variable whose name matches an uppercase pattern: `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `[redacted:envvar]` (with or without the underscore), `[redacted:envvar]`, `[redacted:envvar]` and `CREDENTIAL`.
  - The names are computed from the environment at each call, so a variable added later is covered with no edit; the keep-list is empty, because the inventory found no reader inside an agent session.
  - Arguments and the exit status pass through unchanged (`opencode -s <id>`, `run`, `serve`, `attach`).
  - Sockets and paths such as the ssh agent socket, the display authority file and the terminal's public key are not matched.
  - The parent shell keeps its variables, so the clients the user runs himself keep working.
- **A bypass that is explicit**: `command opencode` runs the real binary with the full environment, and is documented as such.
- **Tests** in a scratch directory with synthetic variables, in zsh and in bash, and a live check on a herdr-started agent (count of matching names in the agent process, never the names or values).
- **`AGENTS.md`** gets one line in the Commands section: agents started from a shell run through this function.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `agent-environment`: which variables an agent started from the user's shells may inherit, how the wrapper decides, what it leaves alone, and how that is checked without printing a name or a value.

### Modified Capabilities

--- brief
# Signal to the fleet: the noreply address, and filtering history before publishing


## Origin

Sender: the Neovim configuration repository, change `prepare-public-release` (roadmap session S14), through its orchestrator.
Addressees: the orchestrators of the other repositories of the fleet, for their own decision under their own process.
Nothing here is an instruction: each repository decides.


## What this repository learned

Measured on this repository's history (counts only, 2026-11-16) before it goes public:

- Every commit carried the user's identity e-mail address, and the merge commits made by the hosting service's command line also carried the full name. Both are public the day the repository is.
- The history held private terms (names of clients, private folders and private repositories) in old versions of documents and transcripts, although the current tree was clean: a scan of the tree does not see them.
- A secret scanner (gitleaks 8.30.1, pinned with `mise exec`, no global install) found nothing in all refs: it looks for credentials, not for names.
- The hosting service keeps `refs/pull/<n>/head` for every merged pull request. After a force-push, the old commits stay reachable by URL and by SHA until the service's support removes those refs.


## What we ask each repository to review

01. **The noreply address.** Turn on "Keep my email addresses private" in the account settings, set `user.name` to the login and `user.email` to `<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com` (the id comes from `gh api user`) in the repository configuration, and note it in the repository's rules. The setting does not touch commits already made.
01. **Existing history, before the first publication.** Scan every ref with the pinned scanner, and run the project's own private-term check on `git log -p --all` and on the commit messages (counts only, in the redaction tool's own report). If anything is found, decide between filtering the history, publishing a fresh repository, or accepting it; record the decision.
01. **Filtering, if chosen.** One pass of `git filter-repo` on a bare scratch clone, never on a working repository. The script of this repository (`history_filter.py`, next to this brief) is an example; it needs the redaction tool of this repository and a store laid out like ours. The method:
    - a file callback that redacts every version of a document with the project's rules, loaded at run time from the private store, with no term in the script;
    - a mailmap, or name and e-mail callbacks, for the identity;
    - the old refs saved first in a `git bundle` (mode 0700, never pushed) with the list of their SHAs, then pushed ref by ref with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<old sha>` under the user's explicit approval;
    - checks before the push: the rewritten branch has the same tree as before, no private term in any diff or message, a clean scan of all refs, every address is the noreply one.
01. **The pull request refs.** Ask the hosting service's support to remove them, and do not change the visibility before they confirm, unless the user accepts the risk.


## Provenance

Sent through the orchestrator of the Neovim repository's sessions, with the user's decision of 2026-11-09 (the noreply address for every commit, and the same filtering for the fleet).
Nothing was changed in any other repository.

--- the function (source)
## opencode without the secret-named variables of the shell

# An agent can print its environment, and what it prints ends up in its transcript.
# The agent does not need the secrets: its providers come from its own login file.
# So `opencode` is a function that runs the real binary through `env -u NAME`
# for every exported variable whose name matches the pattern below.
#
# - The names are read from the environment at each call: no list lives in this file,
#   and a variable added later is covered with no edit.
# - Only the child is affected: the shell keeps its variables.
# - Arguments and exit status pass through unchanged.
# - Explicit bypass, typed by the user: `command opencode` runs the real binary
#   with the full environment. There is no switch an agent could set from its shell.
# - `command env ... opencode` looks the binary up on PATH, so the function
#   does not call itself.
# - The command substitution is split into words by bash and by zsh;
#   the names hold only letters, digits and underscores.
# - Uppercase names only: lowercase and mixed-case names are not matched.
opencode() {
  command env $(env | sed -n 's/^\([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\)=.*/\1/p' \
    | grep -E '(TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|API_?KEY|ACCESS_?KEY|PRIVATE_?KEY|CREDENTIAL)' \
    | sed 's/^/-u /') opencode "$@"
}

# vim: set syntax=sh :

=== proposal.md
## Why
An interactive zsh takes about 2.5 s to start and a login zsh about 7 s, and tmux opens login shells, so every new pane waits that long.
Startup also prints banners and an error, builds a long and partly duplicated `PATH`, forces a locale that is not generated, fails to load at all for bash login shells on a bare terminal, and exports every API token to every process (audit findings F06, F18 to
## What Changes
- Login shells load `rc.d` once: `profile` sets the environment only and no longer sources the interactive rc (F06).
- Completions that cost more than a few tens of milliseconds are cached in files regenerated when their tool changes, or loaded lazily; `brew completions link` leaves startup; the four `chezmoi source-path` calls become one (F19).
- `PATH` is built by prepending to the inherited value without duplicates; `~/.local/bin` comes first; the aqua directory bug is fixed (F18).
- The infracost completion call is fixed (F20).
- Locale defaults use generated locales and no longer force `LC_ALL` (F21).
- bash login shells find the shared rc without `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set; empty globs no longer error (F22).
- API tokens are no longer exported to every shell: exposure becomes opt-in, through a mechanism chosen with the user (F23).
- Banners become debug output; compinit runs once; syntax highlighting loads last; the shell umask is decided (F33).
## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
- `shell-startup`: how fast and how cleanly bash and zsh start, and what environment they provide.
### Modified Capabilities
None.
## Impact
- `dot_config/shell/` (`profile`, `shellrc`, `rc.d/*`, `aliases`), `dot_config/bash/bashrc`, `dot_config/zsh/zshrc`, possibly a new `~/.zshenv`.
- New cache directory for generated completions (under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
- Tools that relied on tokens in the environment need the chosen loader.

=== design.md
## Context
See the audit, section 2.6 (load order) and findings F06, F18 to F23, F33, with measured costs in F19.
Measured on 2026-10-30: `zsh -i -c exit` 2.5 to 3.6 s, `zsh -l -i -c exit` 7.0 s; tmux `default-shell` is `/bin/zsh`, which starts login shells.
## Goals / Non-Goals
**Goals:**
- Interactive zsh startup at most 1.0 s (median of 5), login shells within 10 % of it.
- Silent, error-free startup.
- Predictable `PATH` and locale.
**Non-Goals:**
- New aliases (change `port-[redacted:private]-shell-aliases`).
- Changing the prompt or plugins beyond load order.
## Decisions
### Profile is environment-only
`profile` exports `CURRENT_SHELL`, XDG and `PATH`-related variables, and sources nothing interactive; `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc` keep loading `shellrc`.
For bash login shells, `profile` sources `~/.bashrc` when interactive (Debian's convention), since bash reads only one of them.
### Cached completions
A helper `_cached_completion <tool> <command...>` writes the completion script to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/shell/completions/<shell>/<tool>` when missing or older than the tool's binary (`[ "$bin" -nt "$file" ]`), then sources it.
Alternative considered: lazy wrappers per command (define a stub that loads the completion on first use); kept for tools whose completion is slow to generate and rarely used (localstack).
### Token exposure (to confirm with the user first)
Options:
- a loader function (`secrets on`) that sources the encrypted environment into the current shell only;
- per-directory loading through direnv or mise `[env]` with age-encrypted values;
- per-command wrappers for the few tools that need a token.
Default proposal: loader function plus wrappers for `gh` and the AI tools; nothing exported at startup.
### Shell umask
Options: keep 002, align with chezmoi's 027, or Debian's 022; decided with the user in this session, applied in `profile`.
## Risks / Trade-offs
- [Risk] Tools that read tokens from the environment break silently. → List them first (`grep` the token variable names locally in tool configs); test each.
- [Risk] Cached completions go stale after an upgrade that keeps the binary's mtime. → Cache key includes the tool's `--version` output hash when cheap.
- [Risk] Removing `LC_ALL` changes the language of messages and sorting. → Set `LANG` and the `LC_*` categories explicitly to generated locales; compare `locale` before and after.
## Open Questions
- Token exposure mechanism (above).
- Shell umask value.
- Generate `en_US.UTF-8` (needs sudo) or default to `fr_FR.UTF-8` for `LANG` with English messages through `LANGUAGE`?

## Cached completion scripts

# A tool prints its completion script from a command that costs tens to thousands of milliseconds
# (localstack about 1.6 s). Running it at every start made the shell wait for it every time.
#
#   _cached_completion <tool> <command...> && . "$_CC_FILE"
#
# - <tool> is the command to find on PATH; <command...> prints its completion script for the current shell,
#   for example `kubectl completion "$CURRENT_SHELL"`.
# - The script lives in $XDG_CACHE_HOME/shell/completions/<shell>/<tool>; _CC_FILE is set to it, and the
#   caller sources it at the top level, because `source` inside a function would make the top-level
#   `typeset`/`local` statements of a completion script local to the function in zsh.
# - The file is used while the tool still resolves to the file it was made for (first line,
#   `[ -ef ]`: no subprocess) and is not newer than the cache file. A brew upgrade or a mise install moves
#   the link to a new directory, so the next start regenerates. A tool replaced in place with an older
#   modification time, or behind a mise shim, keeps its file until SHELL_COMPLETION_REFRESH=1 or until the
#   directory is deleted: the scripts ask the tool for completions when TAB is pressed, so they stay correct.
# - Generation is silent and goes through a temporary file moved into place, so a shell that starts
#   at the same moment never sources a half-written file. A command that fails or prints nothing caches
#   nothing, and an older file stays in use.
# - SHELL_RC_DEBUG prints one line on standard error for each regeneration.
# shellcheck disable=SC3043

## Why
`fast-correct-shell-startup` was narrowed on 2026-11-16 to the part that makes shell startup silent and fast.
What it left out is the half that decides what environment a shell provides: `PATH`, locale, which secrets are exported and to whom, the shell's umask, and what a non-interactive login shell (the desktop session) loads.
Audit findings F18, F21, F23 and the environment points of F33.
This change is a proposal only: no design, no tasks, nothing applied yet.
## What moves in
From the draft of `fast-correct-shell-startup`, with their open questions:
- **Clean `PATH`** (F18): the requirement "Clean PATH" and the task "`PATH` helper (prepend without duplicates, keep inherited); `.local/bin` first; aqua fix".
- **Working locale** (F21): the requirement "Working locale" and the task "Locale defaults (no `LC_ALL`; no `setlocale` warning)".
- **Opt-in token exposure** (F23): the requirement "Opt-in token exposure" and the task "Token loader as decided; tools that need tokens tested".
  It is also the backlog study "Secrets held by the desktop session" in `TODO.md`, which says what the study must settle before any change.
- **Decisions to take with the user** (task 1.2 of the draft): the token exposure mechanism, the shell umask, the locale.
- **Smaller points of F33**: syntax highlighting loads last, the shell umask is decided.
- **The interactive guard of `shellrc`** (task 2.2 of the draft): it is commented out, and restoring it as drafted would stop the desktop session from loading anything, see below.
Bash login on a bare terminal (F22) stayed in `fast-correct-shell-startup`.
## What the review of 2026-11-16 found for this change
- **The desktop session is a login shell of this configuration.**
  The display manager runs `zsh /etc/sddm/Xsession`, which sources `~/.zprofile` (the same file as `~/.profile`) without being interactive, and the environment it leaves goes to the systemd user manager: every graphical process inherits wha
  `fast-correct-shell-startup` leaves that pass as it is, so the session's environment does not change under it.
- **A better version of "`profile` is environment-only"** is the main design question here.
  As drafted it would give the desktop login a pass of about 40 ms instead of several seconds, but the session would lose what the interactive parts set (mise on `PATH`, tool variables), the private environment file would stay exported ther
  The user wants the better version designed here, together with the token study.
- **`rc.d/040-env_path_base.sh` replaces `PATH`** instead of keeping the inherited value, so the draft requirement "keep inherited entries" does not describe today's behaviour; the second pass of a login shell hid this because it started fr
- **The live `rc.d` has two files that the source does not manage**; one of them is an old copy of `050-env_path_user.sh`, which prepends the user's bin directories a second time.
- **`rc.d/020-env_defaults.sh` forces `LC_ALL`**, and defaults `LANG` to `en_US.UTF-8`, which is not generated here: a shell started without `LANG` (`env -i`, a bare terminal, ssh) makes bash print `setlocale` warnings.
  The tests of `fast-correct-shell-startup` set `LANG` as the desktop session does, so this case stays out of their counts.
## Open questions (carried over)
- Token exposure mechanism: a loader function sourcing the encrypted file in the current shell only, per-directory loading through direnv or mise `[env]`, per-command wrappers, or the key files and keyring options of the backlog study.

- `chezmoi managed`, `chezmoi unmanaged <dir>`, `chezmoi doctor`.
