- Testing a script without running it: render it with `chezmoi -S <worktree> execute-template < home/.chezmoiscripts/<script>.tmpl`, then run the text with `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`, which makes every script print the change it would make instead of making it (read-only queries still run).
  Never set that variable on `chezmoi apply`: chezmoi records a script as run once it exits 0, so the real apply would skip it afterwards.
  The helper warns when it sees both.
- The proof of a script is a harness kept outside the repository (`/tmp/opencode/scripts-test` during `make-install-scripts-idempotent`):
  - isolated mode puts stubs for `sudo`, `apt-get`, `brew`, `pipx`, `mise`, `kubectl`, `codium`, `vim` and the others first on `PATH`, points `HOME` at a scratch directory and reads standard input from `/dev/null`, so a script can only call stubs that log their arguments;
  - live read-only mode lets an allow-list of read-only queries reach the real tools and refuses and logs everything else, with `sudo` always a logging stub;
  - a script passes when it exits 0 and both logs are empty.
- Scripts look for their tools in the directories of `tools.search` (`home/.chezmoidata/tools.yaml`); to add directories or replace the list on one machine, set `extra` or `override` in the local config under `[data.tools.search]`, never in the data file.

- `openspec validate --all --strict`: check specs and changes.
- `mise run hooks:install`: after a fresh clone, install the pre-commit secret scan as a `.git/hooks` shim, which every git version runs.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run one rendered script under the harness.
#   run.sh -m isolated|live [-n name] [-f fixtures-dir] [-s FROM=TO]... [-e VAR=VALUE]... [-a tool]... [-x refuse-exit] [-u sudo-exit] [-P] 
# isolated: stubs only, scratch HOME (copy of fixtures-dir/home when present), answers from fixtures-dir/<tool>.
# live:     real HOME; read-only calls reach the real tools, everything else is refused and logged (see stub).
# -s: text substitution applied to a copy of the script (used for absolute system paths such as the limits file).
# -a: leave this tool out of PATH (tool missing).
# -K: isolated mode only: keep the scratch HOME of the previous run with the same -n (state a fixture wrote there), reset every log.
# -E: isolated mode only: the sudo stub logs, then runs the command as the plain user (for writes aimed at a scratch path via -s).
# HOMEBREW_PREFIX is always passed (live: the real one; isolated: a scratch prefix without bin/brew), as a shell that ran `brew shellenv` ha
# `brew shellenv` prepends the real brew directory to PATH, ahead of the stubs, so scripts must never evaluate it here.
# -P: leave HOMEBREW_PREFIX unset (tests of load_brew); refused when the script embeds the real prefix.
# Exit status: the script's. Logs: out/logs/<name>/{calls.log,sudo.log,refused.log,out.log,status}.

--- the machine-lifecycle test infra change: is there overlap (scope line)
## Why

# T-068: `.state/`, the git-ignored home of orchestration state (interim layout)
## Goal
Give the state of an orchestration session (briefs sent to workers, an append-only journal, evidence, scratch) a home that is inside the checkout, survives a reboot, is readable without a permission prompt, and is never committed or linted.
Today that state goes to `/tmp/opencode/`, which is volatile, outside every session's directory and unnamed.
This micro-task adopts the layout as an experiment, one `.gitignore` line plus the first journal, and records the reasoning so that the task which norms it (`T-069`) and the sibling repos that will port it (`[redacted:private]` phase 8, `bosco`) start fr
## Context digest (self-sufficient: no prior session context required)
- **Origin.**
  The repo orchestrator `[redacted:private]-orch` (opencode session `ses_e633b719cffeUqI3augjsl6tpc`, herdr pane `w9:pC`) was asked on 2026-11-07 to run each darse task in its own worktree under `[redacted:worktrees_root]/`, through herdr, and to look at how two sib
  - `~/.config/nvim`: a coordinator `nvim-orch`, briefs kept in OpenSpec change directories, a telemetry file under `~/.local/state/orchestration/`.
  - `opencode-readonly-guard`: a coordinator `rog-orch`, which during that session was moving its scratch from `/tmp/opencode/rog/` to `<repo>/.state/<agent>/` (`briefs/`, `bin/`, `evidence/`, `notes/`, `tmp/` mode 0700, an append-on
- **The user's directions** (2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08, in the plan phase of that session):
  - Briefs and orchestration state need a lasting home, and `.state/` is where `rog-orch` is experimenting.
  - It may later belong to the planned per-task directories (`[redacted:private]:B-128`, the OpenSpec change-directory pattern): the repo orchestrator keeps the root `.state/` of the main checkout to steer the crew of the whole repository, and each task 
  - Done as a micro-task so that a lasting record of this work exists.
- **Why the ignore rule is a `.gitignore` line, not `.git/info/exclude`.**
  `markdownlint-cli2`'s `gitignore: true` (`.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`, `T-057`) reads `.gitignore` files only, never `.git/info/exclude` nor `core.excludesFile` (measured at `T-057`).
  A `.state/` excluded only through `.git/info/exclude` would be linted by `lint:md` as soon as it holds a brief, and `validate` would fail.
  An unanchored `.state/` pattern matches at any depth, so one line covers the root and a future `project/tasks/<task>/.state/`.
  `lint:secrets` (`hk check --all`) scans the files git lists, so ignored files are not scanned; a brief or journal must therefore never hold a secret, and `T-063`'s rule on session exports does not reach it.
- **Permission boundary (why the location matters).**
  opencode asks before reading or writing outside the session's directory; the global configuration allows only `~/.config/opencode/get-shit-done/*` as an external directory.
  A worker in a worktree under `[redacted:worktrees_root]/` that must read a brief kept in the orchestrator's `darse:.state/` would stop at a permission dialog nobody attends (the `chezmoi-wtasks` incident recorded in `[redacted:repo]`'s roadmap).
  The orchestrator is attended, so a brief is written into the recipient's own `.state/briefs/` and the prompt that points at it carries an absolute path inside the recipient's checkout.
  Whether a same-repository worktree counts as an external directory for opencode is not established; it is measured at the first launch (`T-065`) and recorded.
- **Facts about worktree removal** (expected, to be verified at the first close).
  `git worktree remove` removes a worktree whose only extra files are git-ignored (ignored files are not "untracked" for it), so a task team's `.state/` would be deleted with its worktree, silently.

# Signal brief: darse T-070 (hk upgrade), for dotfiles

Written by `[redacted:private]-orch` (herdr pane `w9:pC`) on 2026-11-17.
A signal, not a work order: `dotfiles` is sole judge of what it does with it (`darse:spec/drs/DR-016-cross_repo_execution_and_dispatch_model.md`).
Nothing here is urgent, and darse writes nothing in your repository.
Confirm it with your user before acting on any of it.
The brief holds no secret value.

## Why you receive it

`dotfiles` pins hk `2.10.0` (`mise.toml`), installs its hook per repository with `hk install --legacy` (`hooks:install`, your audit item F12), and a lead of yours works in a linked worktree of `dotfiles`.
darse changed its own hk pin and measured several things about hk that touch that setup.

## What darse did

- Merged `darse:project/tasks/T-070-hk_upgrade_or_replacement.md` into `dev` (merge `61c2c90`, `dev` at `22afe39`, pushed 2026-11-17); no release, no tag.
- hk stays darse's hook manager and moves from `1.56.1` to the exact pin `2.11.1` (`darse:spec/drs/DR-008-stack_defaults.md` 1.2.0).

## What darse measured (scratch repositories, then darse itself; git 2.53.0 and 2.55.0)

- Below hk `2.8.1` the stash entry sits on `refs/stash`, shared by every linked worktree; `1.56.1` silently lost unstaged edits when two worktrees committed at once (`jdx/hk#1746`).
  From `2.8.1` the entry is on a private ref and the lock is per worktree.
  Your `2.10.0` is above that line, but darse only load-probed `2.9.0` and `2.10.0` (all steps selected the same files as on `1.56.1`); the full matrix ran on `2.8.0`, `2.8.1` and `2.11.1`.
- Residual on every line from `2.8.1` to `2.11.1` (`jdx/hk#1825`): a `git stash` pushed and dropped in another worktree while a hook runs can make hk refuse a commit; nothing is lost.
  It matters to you only where something runs `git stash` in a worktree of `dotfiles`.
- `hk install --legacy` installs nothing when hk is configured globally (`hk install --global`), in `1.56.1` as in `2.11.1`; `--force-local` closes it (`jdx/hk#1826`).
- Full table and evidence: the Resolution of `darse:project/tasks/T-070-hk_upgrade_or_replacement.md`.

## A correction to darse's own record

darse's records named `dotfiles` as the case of a global hk install.
That was an inference of darse's study, not a fact: checked read-only on 2026-11-17, no `hook.*` entry exists in the global or system git configuration of this machine, and your own audit says the hook is a per-repository shim.
So `--force-local` is not a fix you need today; it only matters if someone runs `hk install --global`.
darse corrects its record (`darse:project/tasks/T-070-hk_upgrade_or_replacement.md`, changelog).

## What it means for dotfiles

Probably nothing urgent.
Three optional points:

- `hooks:install` could take `--legacy --force-local` to match darse's installers (`darse:spec/contracts/CT-011-secret_guard_requirements.md` R18); on this machine the result is the same today.
- If you move your pin, `2.11.1` is the line darse measured end to end.
- hk `2.x` refuses a project that carries a `.hkrc.pkl`; you have none.

## Assistant (Build · Claude Sonnet 5.5 · 8.2s)

Good idea, and I sent it to the builder as a refinement of the cut instruction. It is queued, because the builder is working.

**Why it is safe**
- **Per-run settings:** I checked `tests/run.sh` and `tests/mutants/run.sh`. Every run takes its own `DOTFILES_TEST_REPORTS`, `DOTFILES_TEST_TMPDIR` and `DOTFILES_TEST_JOBS`, so parallel runs won't overwrite one report or share temp directories.
- **Timing tests:** they are live-only and skipped in a default run, so a loaded CPU can't make the parallel batch flaky.

**What I told it**
- **One parallel batch, one subagent each:**
  - 7.1 serial and `--jobs` in zsh;
  - 7.1 serial and `--jobs` in bash;
  - 7.3, the mutants run;
  - 7.5, the missing-tool and missing-bash skips.
  - Each uses its own report and temp directory under `.state/tmp/s7-<name>/` and 2 or 3 jobs, so the runs don't starve each other.
- **Live run last, alone:** 7.2 runs after the batch is done, serial with 1 job, nothing else running from its side. It measures timing medians, and the home-listing hash and `~/.parallel` are checked before the batch and again after it.
- **Subagent rules:**
  - Read-only on tracked files, with no commits or edits.
  - They never print the environment or any value.
  - They report only counts, failing test names, the `jobs:` line and their report paths.
  - They stop and ask if the guard refuses a command, instead of working around it.
- **Two cross-checks:**
  - The builder must not edit tracked files while the mutants run, or that script's `git status` comparison fails for a reason that isn't the suite.
  - The builder verifies one subagent claim itself before ticking a task.

**What this saves**
- **Context:** TAP output from each run stays in the subagents, which return only counts.
- **Time:** the batch runs about four things at once instead of one after another. The live run is still serial by design.

## Commands

Always from the worktree root, in zsh, with a scratch place inside the worktree so nothing is written outside `$HOME`:

```
export TMPDIR=$PWD/.state/tmp
tests/run.sh                                  # default run: unit and smoke, jobs 8 here, about 2 minutes
mise run test                                 # the same, through mise
DOTFILES_TEST_JOBS=1 tests/run.sh             # serial, about 6 minutes
DOTFILES_TEST_LIVE=1 tests/run.sh             # live run, always serial, about 6.5 minutes (or: mise run test:live)
tests/mutants/run.sh [mutant-id...]           # the nine mutants, about 3 minutes (or: mise run test:mutants)
tests/run.sh tests/unit/aliases.bats          # one file
```

The tool timeout must be long for the full runs (I used 580 to 620 seconds).
A background run is safer: `nohup ... &`, then poll a summary file.
`.state/tmp/seven.sh` is the script of section 7 (two shells, serial, live, mutants; it writes `.state/tmp/seven/summary.txt` and one output and report per run).
`.state/tmp/each.sh FILE [seconds]` runs every test of a file on its own under a timeout; it finds the test that hangs.
Do not run two suites at once when one is the live run, and do not edit tracked files while `tests/mutants/run.sh` runs (it compares `git status` before and after).
`tests/.reports/` holds the last report and is git-ignored.

## Fragile or surprising

- bats 1.14: a test registered with `bats_test_function` is identified by its function and arguments, the description is only the display name and is passed through `eval` (no `$` or backtick in a description); `--count` fails on a duplicate identity.
  `skip` works in `setup_file`.
  The JUnit `<skipped>` element holds the reason as text, not as a `message` attribute.
- `mise` shims: a shim of a tool that is not active in the directory fails, except that it falls back to the next executable of that name on `PATH`; this made the live stub loop on itself for `bat`.
  `rg`, `python3` and `shellcheck` are shims here.
  Inside `home/dot_config/*` a shim errors with an untrusted-config message, so search from the repository root.
- `TMPDIR` inside the worktree means a scratch home inside a repository that has a `mise.toml`: mise walks up, finds it and the real global config, and asks for trust on a terminal (a hang).
  Every shell and sandbox that starts mise sets `MISE_CEILING_PATHS` and friends (`dt_mise_vars`).
- A plain helper must not change the shell options of its caller (`set +e` ... `set -e` made the caller exit silently, found in `dt_harness_run` and `dt_render`).
- `compinit` needs `~/.cache` to write its dump: `dt_prepare_home` creates it.
- The render takes about 4 s cold and is made once per smoke file in `setup_file`; the files render in parallel.
- The nested runs (`harness.bats`, `runner.bats`) copy the suite with `dt_suite_copy` and need `DT_TOOL_BATS`.
- `tests/helpers/bats/load.bash` sources every plain helper, so a syntax error in one fails every file at load.
- The live run reads the real PATH, brew prefix, mise installs and the global mise config; it expects a provisioned laptop (brew, completions linked, eight cached tools installed).
- On a machine where the `rtk` wrapper of this shell rewrites commands, some output is filtered; `rg -rn` means "replace with n".

## Frictions met so far

- `mise install bats` creates a second install under the short name; the pin key is the long name.
- The aqua entry of bats-core has no checksum although the design assumed one.
- The shellcheck shim is dead in the worktree.
- `git commit | head` kills git on SIGPIPE in the middle of the hook; the commit is not made.
- Shellcheck: the info-level notes also give a non-zero status; SC2329 is a false positive for a function called only from a trap; SC2174, SC2016, SC2088, SC2154, SC2089 and SC2090 needed narrow directives.
- The redaction tool flags literal `/home/` path segments and variable names that contain a secret word; both were renamed.
- bats: the junit formatter fails with "test_result_state: unbound variable" after a broken TAP stream; a duplicate test identity makes `--count` fail.
- A search of `memory/` with the grep tool put large session exports in the context; avoid it.
- zsh: `mapfile` is bash only, a bash helper cannot be sourced from the agent shell, `print` and `=` habits (see `AGENTS.md`).
- The locale of the bare-terminal test prints `setlocale` warnings (counted, not compared).
- herdr: `herdr agent prompt` answers `{id, result}` with no `ok` key; `herdr agent get` shows a null status for the orchestrator.
- The orchestrator's refinement (run section 7 through subagents) arrived after the runs were done from one background script.

116: Orchestration state lives in `.state/` of the checkout, as in the other fleet repositories, not in `/tmp/opencode`: it survives a reboot, an agent reads it without a permission prompt, and it is never committed (the ignore rule is a `.gitignore` line).
117: - `briefs/<name>/`: what an orchestrator sends to an agent.
118:   A brief for an agent that works in a worktree is written into that worktree's own `.state/briefs/`, because an agent that must read outside its own directory stops at a permission prompt nobody answers; the prompt that points at it carries an absolute path inside the worktree.
119: - `tmp/`: scratch of the checkout, mode 0700, for what a session needs and does not keep.
120:   Raw session exports are the exception: they stay in a scratch directory outside the repository until they are redacted and deleted.
121: - `journal.md`: append-only log, one line per event (briefs written, prompts sent, worktrees created and removed, merges, pushes): `- YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS <actor> <event>`.
122: - `git worktree remove` deletes the ignored files of a worktree with it: a brief that must last is copied into its change folder, and nothing else lives only in a worktree's `.state/`.
123: - Ignored files are not scanned by the commit hook, so a brief or a journal never holds a secret value.

# memory/sessions: redacted session transcripts

Transcripts of the agent sessions that worked on this repository.

They are not chezmoi targets: they sit outside `home/`, the source state selected by `.chezmoiroot`.

## Naming

```text
{YYYYMMDDHHMM}-{slug}.md
```

- The timestamp is the session's creation time, local time.
- Sub-agent sessions sit next to their parent; their slug starts with the parent's slug.
- Slugs are neutral on purpose: a file name is not redacted, so it must not carry a name that the text masks.

## Contents

| File | Session | Notes |

profile = "public"
terms = "dotfiles"
check = ["memory/sessions/*.md"]

39:## Redaction
40:
41:The public profile of the redaction tool rewrites each raw export before it enters this repository:
42:
43:1. secrets (API keys, tokens, age secret keys, private key blocks) become `[redacted:secret]`;
44:2. private terms, repository names, credential variable names, token scope lines, IP addresses, e-mail addresses and non-public git hosts become `[redacted:private]`, `[redacted:repo]`, `[redacted:ip]` and similar markers;

46:4. home directories become `~`; `/home/linuxbrew` (Homebrew's prefix) and the placeholder `/home/user` stay.
47:

55:Words from the user's private spell lists in the store count as private terms too, so a plain word written there is masked in every export, compound words included; a public word belongs in the public list of the Neovim configuration repository.
56:The tool and the store are recorded in the user's private notes; the tool is transitional.

58:Redaction only knows what it is told.
59:Before committing, run the tool's `--check` on the redacted files, run the repository's secret scan on `memory/sessions/`, and search the files for what this export is known to be about; none of these is proof on its own.

<content>
1: ## Why
2: 
3: `fast-correct-shell-startup` was narrowed on 2026-11-16 to the part that makes shell startup silent and fast.
4: What it left out is the half that decides what environment a shell provides: `PATH`, locale, which secrets are exported and to whom, the shell's umask, and what a non-interactive login shell (the desktop session) loads.
5: Audit findings F18, F21, F23 and the environment points of F33.
6: This change is a proposal only: no design, no tasks, nothing applied yet.
7: 
8: ## What moves in
9: 
10: From the draft of `fast-correct-shell-startup`, with their open questions:
11: 
12: - **Clean `PATH`** (F18): the requirement "Clean PATH" and the task "`PATH` helper (prepend without duplicates, keep inherited); `.local/bin` first; aqua fix".
13: - **Working locale** (F21): the requirement "Working locale" and the task "Locale defaults (no `LC_ALL`; no `setlocale` warning)".
14: - **Opt-in token exposure** (F23): the requirement "Opt-in token exposure" and the task "Token loader as decided; tools that need tokens tested".
15:   It is also the backlog study "Secrets held by the desktop session" in `TODO.md`, which says what the study must settle before any change.
16: - **Decisions to take with the user** (task 1.2 of the draft): the token exposure mechanism, the shell umask, the locale.
17: - **Smaller points of F33**: syntax highlighting loads last, the shell umask is decided.
18: - **The interactive guard of `shellrc`** (task 2.2 of the draft): it is commented out, and restoring it as drafted would stop the desktop session from loading anything, see below.
19: 
20: Bash login on a bare terminal (F22) stayed in `fast-correct-shell-startup`.
21: 
22: ## What the review of 2026-11-16 found for this change
23: 
24: - **The desktop session is a login shell of this configuration.**
25:   The display manager runs `zsh /etc/sddm/Xsession`, which sources `~/.zprofile` (the same file as `~/.profile`) without being interactive, and the environment it leaves goes to the systemd user manager: every graphical process inherits what `rc.d` exports, tokens included.
26:   `fast-correct-shell-startup` leaves that pass as it is, so the session's environment does not change under it.
27: - **A better version of "`profile` is environment-only"** is the main design question here.
28:   As drafted it would give the desktop login a pass of about 40 ms instead of several seconds, but the session would lose what the interactive parts set (mise on `PATH`, tool variables), the private environment file would stay exported there, and a shell-local guard is needed so the environment part does not run twice in an interactive login shell.
29:   The user wants the better version designed here, together with the token study.
30: - **`rc.d/040-env_path_base.sh` replaces `PATH`** instead of keeping the inherited value, so the draft requirement "keep inherited entries" does not describe today's behaviour; the second pass of a login shell hid this because it started from the same base.
31: - **The live `rc.d` has two files that the source does not manage**; one of them is an old copy of `050-env_path_user.sh`, which prepends the user's bin directories a second time.
32: - **`rc.d/020-env_defaults.sh` forces `LC_ALL`**, and defaults `LANG` to `en_US.UTF-8`, which is not generated here: a shell started without `LANG` (`env -i`, a bare terminal, ssh) makes bash print `setlocale` warnings.
33:   The tests of `fast-correct-shell-startup` set `LANG` as the desktop session does, so this case stays out of their counts.
34: 
35: ## Open questions (carried over)
36: 
37: - Token exposure mechanism: a loader function sourcing the encrypted file in the current shell only, per-directory loading through direnv or mise `[env]`, per-command wrappers, or the key files and keyring options of the backlog study.
38: - Shell umask: keep 002, align with chezmoi's 027, or Debian's 022.
39: - Locale: generate `en_US.UTF-8` (needs sudo, needs the user's go) or default `LANG` to a locale that exists with English messages through `LANGUAGE`.
40: - What a non-interactive login shell loads, and whether `shellrc` gets its interactive guard back once the desktop session no longer depends on it.
41: - Order: it should run after the study of secrets held by the desktop session, or include it.
42: 
43: ## Capabilities
44: 
45: ### New Capabilities
46: 
47: - `shell-environment`: which environment a shell provides (`PATH`, locale, exported secrets, umask) and what each kind of shell loads.
48: 
49: ### Modified Capabilities
50: 
51: None.
52: 
53: ## Impact
54: 
55: - `home/dot_config/shell/` (`profile`, `shellrc`, `rc.d/0*`, `rc.d/020`, `rc.d/930`), possibly a managed `~/.zshenv`.
56: - Tools that read tokens from the environment, and the desktop session's inherited environment.
57: - Depends on `fast-correct-shell-startup` (load order, single pass) and on the credential decisions already taken: the wrapper `add-agent-env-wrapper` stays as it is.
58:

domain `chezmoi:spec` for the change artifacts, `shell` for code), commit only after the user validates it, with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN HK_STASH=none /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/git commit`, and never `git commit | head`.\n  Never push.\n- Anything that uses sudo, writes outside `$HOME`, installs, uninstalls or deletes needs the user's explicit go.\n- Your scratch and logs go in `.state/tmp/` of your worktree, not in `/tmp/opencode`; `.state/journal.md` is the orchestrator's, do not write to it.\n- In every herdr listing, select fields with `jq` (name, status, pane id, tab id); herdr JSON nests agent fields under `.result.agent`, tab fields under `.result.tab`, and `herdr pane read` output is not JSON.\n- Cut your session at a section boundary when your context nears 70%: write a hand-off note into `.state/briefs/correct-shell-environment/` and tell the orchestrator; a fresh session continues from it.\n\n## Reporting\n\n- Report with one short line each time, at five points: reading done, study done (with counts, no names), decisions taken, artifacts ready for review (with the validation result), blocked (say on what).\n  Send it with `herdr agent prompt chezmoi-orch \"<one line>\"` when `herdr agent get chezmoi-orch` succeeds.\n  Agent names can be lost when herdr restarts: when that fails, find the pane of the tab labelled `orch` in the workspace of this repository (`herdr tab list --workspace <id>`, then `herdr agent list` with `jq`) and prompt it by pane id, checking the tab label before you rely on it.\n  `herdr agent prompt` refuses a blocked agent: when the orchestrator waits for the user, write the line in your own pane as well.\n- Keep a list of every friction you meet with the tooling, and send it with the last report.\n- When a command or diagnostic of yours makes a private value inferable in your transcript, say so in the report, so that the export of your session is masked before it is committed.\n- Your session export is done at the end, when the user asks, following `memory/sessions/README.md`.\n\n<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->\n"
}

118: 
119: - The interactive shell of an agent holds 69 entries, the user manager 62.
120: - Two duplicates in both, `~/.local/bin` and `~/.local/sbin`, come from the unmanaged live `190-env_path_user.sh`, a copy of `050`; the scratch render, without that file, has none.
121: - `040-env_path_base.sh` replaces `PATH`, so a nested shell does not grow it, but it also drops what the parent added (mise's directories are added again by mise).
122: - `120-pkg-aqua.sh` appends `/bin` to an inherited `AQUA_BIN_DIR`: one more level per nested shell (`bin/bin/bin` in an agent's shell, measured in nested bash on the render); aqua's root directory does not exist on the laptop, so the entry is missing at every level.
123: - mise's activation puts its tool directories first at every prompt: `~/.local/bin` is at position 54 in an agent's shell, behind 50 mise directories, so a requirement that it comes first cannot hold while mise is activated.
124: - Five commands of `~/.local/bin` also exist elsewhere on `PATH`; putting `~/.local/bin` before brew would change the one that runs for one of them.
125: 
126: ## Locale
127: 
128: - Generated: `C`, `C.utf8`, `fr_FR.utf8` (and `POSIX`); `/etc/default/locale` sets `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`.
129: - The login modules of the console, ssh, cron, su and the display manager read `/etc/default/locale`, so those sessions start with `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`; `020` then forces `LC_ALL=fr_FR.UTF-8` and defaults `LANGUAGE` to `en_US`.
130: - `LANGUAGE=en_US` already gives English messages, and the forced `LC_ALL` defeats the `man` alias of the aliases file (`LANG=C man`): `LANG=C date` still prints a French day name.
131: - A shell started without `LANG` (`env -i bash -i`, `env -i bash -l -i`) gets `LANG=en_US.UTF-8`, which is not generated, and prints 4 `setlocale` warnings for `LC_CTYPE` and `LC_COLLATE` while `330-shell_completion.sh` loads bash-completion, which clears `LC_ALL` for a moment; zsh prints none.
132: - An ssh client that sends `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8` (sshd accepts `LANG` and `LC_*`) makes an interactive bash print 7 `setlocale` warnings, because `020` keeps an inherited `LC_ALL`.
133: - Removing only the forced `LC_ALL` while keeping the `en_US.UTF-8` default makes a child program warn in a shell started without `LANG` (perl, measured).
134: 
135: ## umask
136: 
137: - The system's login modules set it: `pam_umask` with per-user groups (`USERGROUPS_ENAB yes`) gives 0002 to every login, the user manager included, and every process of the session has 0002 except speech-dispatcher (0007).
138: - The graphical processes are services of the user manager, so a `umask` in the desktop pass of `profile` would reach `startplasma-x11` and not the applications; a shell umask changes shells and what they start.
139: - The user's private group has no other member, so 002 and 022 grant the same access in practice; three human accounts have a login shell, and the home directory is mode 0755, so files that are world-readable are readable by the other accounts: 224 of the 554 files in the first two levels of `~/.config`.
140: - The mode drift under `~/.config/shell` predates chezmoi's umask 027: the 30 files at 0664 were last written before 2026-11-08, the 11 files applied since are 0640.
141: 
142: ## Corrections to the proposal and the brief
143: 
144: - The draft spec of `shell-environment` existed, moved unchanged from `fast-correct-shell-startup`.
145: - `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply` (tasks 2.3 and 2.4) owns both unmanaged `rc.d` files; `190` is identical to `050`.
146: - The `setlocale` warnings of a shell started without `LANG` are real in bash, through bash-completion; the console, ssh and cron do not start without `LANG`.
147: - The scenario "User bin first" of the draft spec cannot hold while mise is activated.
148: - The shell umask does not decide the umask of the desktop session or of the user manager.
149: - `shell/environment` is not unused material: it is the loader of an environment-only pass.

19: ## Goals / Non-Goals

21: **Goals:**

24: - The desktop login loads the environment the session uses and nothing interactive.

31:

38: ## Decisions
39: 
40: The five decisions were taken with the user on 2026-11-21, one at a time, with the options below.
41: 
42: ### 1. Keys on demand: a `secrets` function, per-tool keys as the target
43: 
44: - `rc.d/010-env_user.sh` keeps `envrc` and the `unset` of the revoked GitHub variable, and stops sourcing the private file.
45: - A new interactive-only file, `rc.d/446-tools_secrets.sh`, defines `secrets`:
46:   - `secrets load` sources the private file into the calling shell and exports a marker, `DOTFILES_SECRETS=loaded`;
47:   - `secrets unload` unsets every name the file sets;
48:   - `secrets` alone prints how many of the file's names are set, a count and never a name.
49: - When it is sourced at the start of an interactive shell without the marker, the file unsets the names of the private file that the shell inherited: terminals and multiplexers started by the old session hold them until the next login.
50:   With the marker, the shell is a child of a shell that loaded them on purpose, and keeps them.
51:   The names are read from the file at each call, as the `opencode` function does: no name is written in the repository.
52: - The marker matches the secret pattern, so the `opencode` function removes it with the keys, and a shell started inside an agent unsets nothing it does not hold.
53: - Alternatives considered:
54:   - interactive shells keep loading the file and only the desktop stops: it protects the desktop and leaves every terminal and every agent other than opencode with every key (F23 unchanged);
55:   - per-directory loading (direnv `.envrc` or mise `[env]`): it fits cem and the fleet repository, not the general tools that run anywhere; it stays possible later, an `.envrc` can call `secrets load`;
56:   - per-tool keys now: best isolation, but configured tool by tool, for configurations that live in other repositories or are not managed yet.
57: - Follow-ups, the target: a key command or a key file of mode 0600 per tool (`secret-tool` reads the wallet that `pam_kwallet` opens at login): a note to the Neovim repository for avante, whose key names accept `cmd:`; `manage-ai-tool-configs` for the command-line client that has a key-command setting; the VSCodium extension's own key setting if it is ever used again.
58: 
59: ### 2. umask 027 for the user's sessions, 022 for sudo, home 0700, from one install script
60: 
61: - A new script, `run_onchange_before_03-session-defaults.sh.tmpl`, with data under `system.session` in `.chezmoidata/packages.yaml`:
62:   - `umask: "027"`: written as `umask=027` in the `other` sub-field of the user's GECOS field (`chfn -o`, root only), which `pam_umask` reads first; set explicitly there, it is not turned into 007 by `USERGROUPS_ENAB`; the other entries of that sub-field (`pri=`, `ulimit=`) are kept;
63:   - `sudo_umask: "022"`: `/etc/sudoers.d/50-umask` holds `Defaults umask=0022` and `Defaults umask_override`, written to a temporary file, checked with `visudo -cf`, installed with mode 0440;
64:   - `home_mode: "0700"`: `chmod` on `$HOME`, no sudo;
65:   - `locales: [en_US.UTF-8, fr_FR.UTF-8]`: decision 3.
66: - The script follows the install-scripts capability: no-op when everything matches (no sudo call), dry run, non-interactive, never weakens: a stricter umask in GECOS, a stricter home mode or a generated locale that the list does not name are left as they are, with a warning.
67:   On a system without `chfn`, `/etc/sudoers.d` or `locale-gen` it skips that part and says so.
68: - The shell sets no umask: the login does, for shells and graphical applications alike.
69: - Why GECOS: `pam_umask` reads the umask from the GECOS field, its own argument, `UMASK` in `/etc/login.defs` and `/etc/default/login`, nothing else.
70:   `~/.pam_environment` sets variables, the umask is not one, `user_readenv` is deprecated and only the display manager's stack enables it, and the user manager's stack has no `pam_env`; systemd 262 has no per-user default umask.
71:   `UMASK 027` in `login.defs` would change the two other accounts and root.
72: - Why sudo 022: without a umask in sudoers, sudo uses the union of the user's umask and 022, so 027: `sudo cp tool /usr/local/bin/` would give a root:root 0750 file the user cannot run, APT keyrings written with `sudo tee` would be ignored by apt's download user, desktop files under `/usr/local/share/applications` would vanish from the menu.
73: - Alternatives considered: keep 002 (the other accounts read every new world-readable file), 022 (identical to 002 with an empty private group), 027 in interactive shells only (applications keep 0002, and sudo gets 027), home 0700 alone (closes existing files but new files stay world-readable outside the home).
74: 
75: ### 3. Locale: no `LC_ALL`, missing locales dropped, `en_US.UTF-8` generated
76: 
77: - `rc.d/020-env_defaults.sh`:
78:   - sets no `LC_ALL`;
79:   - drops an inherited `LANG`, `LC_ALL` or `LC_*` that names a locale not generated on the machine (one `locale -a`, about 2 ms, names compared without case and without `-`);
80:   - defaults an unset `LANG` to `en_US.UTF-8` when it is generated and to `C.UTF-8` otherwise;
81:   - defaults `LANGUAGE` to `en_US:en`, so messages stay English while formats follow `LANG` (French here, as today).
82: - The script of decision 2 makes sure the locales of `system.session.locales` are generated (`/etc/locale.gen` and `locale-gen`), adding and never removing.
83: - Measured on a prototype of `020` (scratch render, 20 kinds of shell): 0 warnings from the user's files, child programs included; an ssh client sending a missing `LC_ALL` goes from 7 warnings to 1 in `bash -i` and 3 in `bash -l -i`, printed by bash and `/etc/profile` before any user file runs (out of reach: the client or sshd's `AcceptEnv` is the place); zsh prints none.
84: - The `man` alias of the aliases file (`LANG=C man`) works again.
85: - Alternatives considered: generating `en_US.UTF-8` alone (it does not remove the forced `LC_ALL` nor handle a missing inherited locale), dropping `LC_ALL` alone (the `en_US.UTF-8` default then warns in a shell started without `LANG`).
86: 
87: ### 4. The desktop login loads the environment only; `shellrc` is interactive-only again
88: 
89: - The non-interactive branch of `profile` (the desktop session, `zsh -l -c`, `bash -l -c`) sources `shell/environment` instead of `zsh/zshrc` or `bash/bashrc`.
90: - `shell/environment` sources `rc.d/*-env_*.sh`, so the environment is exactly the `env_` files:

93:   | --- | --- |
94:   | `000-env_xdg_dirs.sh` | XDG base directories |
95:   | `010-env_user.sh` | `envrc`, the `unset` of the revoked variable |
96:   | `020-env_defaults.sh` | locale, `EDITOR`, `PAGER` |
97:   | `030-env_current_shell.sh` | `CURRENT_SHELL` |
98:   | `035-env_path_helper.sh` (new) | `_path_prepend` and `_path_clean`, defined in each pass |
99:   | `040-env_path_base.sh` | keeps the inherited `PATH`, appends the missing system directories, drops missing directories and duplicates |
100:   | `041-env_pkg_brew.sh` (from `110`) | `brew shellenv`, the `HOMEBREW_*` settings |
101:   | `042-env_pkg_aqua.sh` (from `120`) | `AQUA_ROOT_DIR`, an inherited `AQUA_BIN_DIR` kept as it is |
102:   | `043-env_pkg_snap.sh` (from `140`) | `/snap/bin` |
103:   | `044-env_pkg_krew.sh` (from `150`) | `KREW_ROOT`, its bin directory |
104:   | `045-env_lang_go.sh` (from `200-lang_go`) | `GOPATH`, `GOBIN` |

109:   `060` stays free for the `060-env_libvirt.sh` that `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply` plans.
110: - `110-pkg_brew.sh` keeps what is interactive: completions, `fpath`, the brew-file wrapper and its commit hook.
111: - `_path_prepend` moves a directory to the front when it is already there and skips one that does not exist, so a nested shell, or a terminal that inherits the session's `PATH`, ends with the same list.
112: - Order of `PATH` after the environment part: the user's bin directories, mise's shims, the package managers and languages, the inherited entries this file does not know, the system directories.
113:   In an interactive shell mise's activation then puts its tool directories first, at every prompt: the draft scenario "`~/.local/bin` first" becomes "the user's bin directories come before every system and package-manager directory".
114:   One command of `~/.local/bin` that brew also provides changes owner on the laptop (measured).
115: - `shellrc` gets its guard back (`case $- in *i*) ;; *) return ;; esac`): no caller sources it non-interactively any more.
116:   A bash run by sshd for a command reads `~/.bashrc`, so ssh commands of a bash user stop loading the interactive configuration (the user's login shell is zsh).
117: - The `case $-` of `profile` is the guard against a second environment pass in an interactive login shell: zsh does nothing in `profile` and reads `~/.zshrc`, bash sources `~/.bashrc`; both run the `env_` files once, through `shellrc`.
118: - Measured on prototypes (scratch render, medians of 7 alternating runs of the replayed desktop call): 0.23 s and 55 exported names, 0 synthetic secrets, the same `PATH` length, against 0.62 s and 108 names today.
119: - Alternatives considered: the full pass minus the private file (106 names, 0.62 s, mise's hook state and the aliases variables still in the user manager, `shellrc` cannot be guarded); the same plus a managed `~/.zshenv` (backlog, below).

121: ### 5. Loose ends of F33
122: 
123: - `930-highlighting.sh` becomes `999-highlighting.sh`: zsh-syntax-highlighting must load after every plugin that defines widgets, and the prompt (`990`) defines one.
124: - Removed: `005-dbg_prof_enable.sh` and `995-dbg_prof_results.sh` (commented-out profiling; `SHELL_RC_DEBUG` and the timing tests replace them), `130-pkg-flatpack.sh` and `200-lang_python.sh` (empty), `~/.config/zsh/zshrc` and `~/.config/bash/bashrc` (decision 4 removes their only caller).
125:   Each removed or renamed target, the old names of the moved `env_` files included, gets an entry in `home/.chezmoiremove`.
126: - `HISTFILE` moves under `$XDG_STATE_HOME`: `zsh/history` and `bash/history`, directories 0700, files 0600.
127:   About 40 live zsh processes share `~/.zsh_history` (`share_history`), so the migration loses nothing:
128:   - the first new shell finds no new file and a regular legacy file, moves it (same file system, an atomic rename) and leaves a symbolic link at the old path;
129:   - running shells append through the link into the new file;
130:   - a running shell that trims its history rewrites the old path as a regular file (zsh writes a copy and renames it over the link); the next shell that starts finds a regular file there again, merges it into the new file (every entry once, in timestamp order, written to a temporary file and moved into place) and puts the link back;
131:   - two shells that start at once: the second one's move, merge or link fails silently and it uses the new file;
132:   - after the reboot no old shell is left, and the link at the old path can go.
133: - `shell/environment` is the loader of decision 4.
134: 
135: ### Load order, before and after
136: 
137: | Kind | Example | Today | After |
138: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
139: | Desktop session | `/etc/sddm/Xsession`, zsh, not interactive | `profile`, `zsh/zshrc`, `shellrc`, all of `rc.d` (private file included) | `profile`, `shell/environment` (`env_` files only), no key |
140: | Interactive zsh | the terminal, multiplexer panes | `shellrc`, all of `rc.d`, private file | `shellrc`, all of `rc.d`, no key until `secrets load`; inherited keys unset unless the marker is set |
141: | Interactive login zsh | `zsh -l -i`, console, ssh login | `profile` (nothing for zsh), then as above | same |
142: | Interactive bash, login or not | `bash -i`, `bash -l -i` | `profile` for a login, `shellrc`, all of `rc.d` | same as zsh |
143: | Non-interactive login | `zsh -l -c`, `bash -l -c` | zsh: all of `rc.d`; bash: nothing (`bash/bashrc` returns) | both: `shell/environment` |
144: | Non-interactive zsh | `zsh -c`, ssh command | `/etc/zsh/zshenv` only | same |
145: | Non-interactive bash | `bash -c` | nothing | same |
146: | bash run by sshd | ssh command, login shell bash | `~/.bashrc` = `shellrc`, all of `rc.d` | `shellrc` returns at once |
147: | `env -i` interactive | `env -i zsh -i` | as interactive, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` (missing), bash warns | as interactive, `LANG=en_US.UTF-8` once generated (else `C.UTF-8`), no warning |

153: - `PATH`: the user's bin directories, mise's shims instead of one directory per mise tool, brew, the language directories, the system directories, no duplicate.
154: - Gone, because only shells use them: the aliases file's variables (`forgit_*`, `LESS_TERMCAP_*`, `FORGIT_INSTALL_DIR`, `KUBECOLOR_*`), `LS_COLORS`, `LESSOPEN`, `LESSCLOSE`, `HSTR_CONFIG`, `MISE_SHELL` and the `__MISE_*` hook state.
155: - Kept: the XDG directories, `EDITOR`, `VISUAL`, `PAGER`, the `HOMEBREW_*` and brew-file settings, `GOPATH`, `KREW_ROOT`, `AQUA_*`, `CURRENT_SHELL`, `envrc`'s variables.

157: - umask 0027 in every process of the session, once the script of decision 2 has run.

159: ### Specifications
160: 
161: - New capability `shell-environment`, replacing the draft moved from `fast-correct-shell-startup`.
162: - `shell-startup`: "Single load of the interactive configuration" and "Behaviour that a startup change must keep" are modified (a non-interactive login shell loads the environment part, and startup no longer exports the private file); the other five requirements stay.
163: - `agent-environment`: "A herdr-started agent holds none of them" is modified (the pane's shell holds the keys only after `secrets load`); the other five stay.
164: - `install-scripts`: one requirement added for the session-defaults script; the others stay.
165: - `shell-test-harness`: "The three ported suites keep their strictness" is modified so the scenario table of `tests/README.md` also maps `shell-environment`; the others stay.
166: - `secret-hygiene`: unchanged; where keys live is `shell-environment`'s business and the per-tool keys are follow-ups.

168: ### Tests
169: 
170: - Smoke tests on the scratch render (`tests/smoke/environment-*.bats`) start the 20 kinds of shell of the study with a synthetic private file of `DEMO_` names, and count: names exported, `rc.d` passes, `PATH` entries, duplicates and missing directories, locale variables, `setlocale` lines, history paths.
171: - Unit tests for `_path_prepend`, the locale filter, the history migration and merge (synthetic history files, multi-line entries), `secrets` in zsh and bash, and the session-defaults script in the isolated harness (stubs for `chfn`, `getent`, `visudo`, `locale-gen`, `install`, `sudo`).
172: - Live tests, read-only and opt-in, for the checks that only a new login proves: the user manager and the terminal hold 0 names of the private file, session processes have umask 0027, no `LC_ALL` in the user manager.
173: - One mutant per requirement in `tests/mutants/`, each making at least one test fail.
174: - The startup tests that expect the private names in new shells and in the desktop replay change meaning; the mutant `startup-unset-removed` is kept against the `unset` line of `010`.

176: ## Risks / Trade-offs
177: 
178: - [Risk] A mistake in `profile` leaves the desktop session without `PATH` or without a usable environment at the next login. → The replay of the display manager's call runs in the smoke tests before and after (`DOTFILES_TEST_BASE_REF`, with the removed names listed in an allow file); `profile` is deployed last; rollback from a text console is one command (`chezmoi apply` of the previous `profile`, or `git checkout` of it and an apply), and the old file's content is in git.
179: - [Risk] A tool used from the desktop needed one of the keys. → The study found one reader, a VSCodium extension that is not running and has its own key setting; a key-reading tool started from a terminal works after `secrets load`.
180: - [Trade-off] The user types `secrets load` before a key-reading tool, and Neovim must be started from a shell that did. → Accepted; the per-tool keys of the follow-ups remove the step tool by tool.
181: - [Risk] The session-defaults script writes outside `$HOME` with sudo: the GECOS field, a sudoers file, `/etc/locale.gen`. → Idempotent and guarded: it compares before writing and calls sudo only to write; the sudoers file is validated with `visudo -cf` before it is installed (a broken sudoers file would lock sudo out); a stricter value is never weakened; dry run first; first run by hand with the user's go, then at the supervised apply.
182: - [Risk] umask 027 makes a file unreadable for another account or a service: containers whose user is not the user's cannot read bind-mounted files, `qemu:///system` cannot read an image kept in the home. → Accepted by the user; none of them exists on the laptop today (0 libvirt domains or pools, 0 Incus instances); virt-manager offers an ACL fix; an `.envrc` or `umask 022` in a shell covers a one-off.
183: - [Risk] `chmod 700 ~` hides a file that another account or service reads from the home. → None found (no ACL, the display manager uses its own copy of the avatar); rollback `chmod 755 ~`.
184: - [Risk] The history migration loses entries while old shells run. → Link at the old path, merge at the next start when a trim turned it back into a file, tests on synthetic files; the legacy file is never replaced before the merged file is in place.
185: - [Risk] A deployed old `rc.d` file and its renamed `env_` copy both run during a partial deployment. → `_path_prepend` drops duplicates; each rename is deployed together with the removal of the old target.
186: - [Trade-off] `120`, `140`, `150`, `200-lang_go` and `220` become `env_` files: five renames in one change. → They are one line of `PATH` each, and the rule "the environment is the `env_` files" is what makes the desktop pass and the tests simple.
187: - [Risk] A future `rc.d` file exports something the desktop needs without being an `env_` file. → The rule is written in `shell/environment` and in the spec; the desktop replay test lists the exported names.
188: - [Limit] The `setlocale` warning that bash or `/etc/profile` prints before any user file runs, when an ssh client sends a missing locale, stays. → Documented; the client or sshd is the place.
189: 
190: ## Migration Plan
191: 
192: 1. Build: tests first, then code, `mise run test` green, `mise run test:mutants` green, shellcheck and `zsh -n` on every changed file.
193: 2. Deploy one target at a time with `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <target>`, each followed by a new interactive shell in a spare tab:
194:    1. `rc.d/035-env_path_helper.sh`, then each renamed `env_` file together with the removal of its old target (the user's go for each deletion);
195:    2. `rc.d/446-tools_secrets.sh`, then `rc.d/010-env_user.sh` (from then on new shells hold no key until `secrets load`);
196:    3. `rc.d/020-env_defaults.sh`, `rc.d/320-shell_history.sh` (the first new shell moves the history), `999-highlighting.sh` with the removal of `930`, the removal of the four stub and empty files;
197:    4. `shellrc`, then `profile` last, with the removal of `zsh/zshrc` and `bash/bashrc`.
198: 3. The session-defaults script: rendered and run with `CHEZMOI_SCRIPTS_DRY_RUN=1`, reviewed, then run by hand by the user in a terminal where sudo asks for the password; `sudo -l` and a test file created with sudo (mode 0644) check the sudoers file at once.
199: 4. Reboot (a full logout is not enough while user services keep the manager alive).
200: 5. Live checks: `mise run test:live`; the counts of the user manager's and the terminal's variables (0 names of the private file, 0 secret-pattern names); `umask` of session processes 0027; `ls -ld ~` 0700; the old history path is a link (then it can be removed).
201: 6. Tick the `TODO.md` reboot check and update the "Secrets held by the desktop session" item when the orchestrator asks.
202: 
203: Rollback: the previous version of each target from git and a single-target apply (`profile` first); `sudo chfn -o '' <user>` (or the previous `other` sub-field, which the script prints in its log), `sudo rm /etc/sudoers.d/50-umask`, `chmod 755 ~`; the generated locale can stay; the history file can be moved back to `~/.zsh_history`.
204: 
205: ## Follow-ups

207: - Per-tool keys (decision 1): a note to the Neovim repository for avante's `cmd:` key names; `manage-ai-tool-configs` for the command-line client with a key-command setting.
208: - Backlog: a managed `~/.zshenv` that loads the environment part for non-interactive non-login zsh (ssh commands, cron, scripts), to be reviewed with its cost on every `zsh -c`.
209: - `reconcile-drift-and-supervised-apply`: adopt the live libvirt file as `060-env_libvirt.sh` (an `env_` file, so the desktop gets it again) and delete the live `190`.
210: 
211: ## Open Questions

  "content": "# Signal brief: read-only guard blocks on assignments inside a child shell string\n\nWritten by `chezmoi-orch` (the orchestrator of the dotfiles repository) on 2026-11-21.\nA signal, not a work order: the receiving repository is sole judge of what it does with it.\nNothing here is urgent, and the dotfiles write nothing in your repository.\nThe brief holds no secret value and no command text: it names events of the guard's own log by time and reason.\n\n## Why you receive it\n\nThe read-only guard belongs to your repository.\nTwo planning agents of the dotfiles repository, on 2026-11-16 and 2026-11-20, were blocked on a command that looks like a false positive.\nBoth were studying how shells start, which means running a child shell with its command in a string, under `env -i` and a scratch home.\nThat is the normal way to observe a startup file without touching the real session, so the pattern will come back every time this repository plans a shell change.\n\n## The events (`events.jsonl`, type `blocked`, agent kind `plan`, times in UTC)\n\n1. 2026-11-16 14:44:45: reason \"a new value for PATH reaches later commands, which inherit it from the environment\".\n   The command ran a child shell with `-c` and its string set `PATH`.\n2. 2026-11-16 14:44:54: the same reason for the lowercase `path`, nine seconds later in the same session: the agent rewrote the command with zsh's tied array and was blocked again.\n3. 2026-11-20 22:13:06: reason \"bash -c: set -a passes assignments to later commands\".\n   The command was `bash -c` with a single-quoted string that began with `set -a`.\n4. 2026-10-29 14:04:48: reason \"systemctl show-environment changes system state\".\n   That subcommand prints the user manager's environment and changes nothing (`set-environment`, `unset-environment` and `import-environment` do).\n   It may have been fixed since; the event is listed so that it can be checked.\n\n## Why the first three look like false positives\n\nAn assignment or `set -a` inside the string of a child shell lives in that child process and ends with it.\nThe agent's own shell never sees it, and no later command inherits it.\nThe reasons quoted above describe a leak into later commands, which holds for a bare assignment in the agent's persistent shell and not for one inside `bash -c '...'` or `zsh -c '...'`.\nWhat the string runs still has to pass the read-only rules.\n\n## What may be worth considering\n\nThese are candidates, not requests.\n\n- Treat the string of a child shell started with `-c` as its own scope: assignments, `export` and `set -a` inside it do not raise the leak reason, while every command inside it is still checked.\n- Keep the reason for a bare assignment at the top level, where the shell is persistent.\n- Check the list of read-only `systemctl` subcommands against the event of 2026-10-29.\n- The guard's own `review` summary already shows 8 blocks on the word `nvim` inside an argument of `gh` (a repository name equal to a command name).\n  If that is not in your backlog, it is the same family: a word inside an argument or a string read as a command.\n\n## What the dotfiles side did meanwhile\n\nThe agents moved their probes into script files that they then ran, which works but costs a step each time and hides the probe from the review of the command.\nNo change is needed on the dotfiles side.\n\n## What chezmoi asks\n\nNothing.\nA reply is welcome only if the item already exists in your backlog (a pointer is enough) or if you decide to take it.\n\n<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->\n"

15: 
16: - The `cmd:` form works as the brief says: a provider's `api_key_name` starting with `cmd:` makes the plugin run the command (through `sh -c`) and take the first line of its output.
17: - It runs when a request needs the key, never at startup. A success is cached for the life of that Neovim process; a failure is reported once and not cached.
18: - It runs synchronously, with no timeout (read in the code, not tested). A command that waits on a dialog, such as a locked wallet, would block Neovim until it is answered. Worth knowing for the choice of key store.
19: - With the `cmd:` form the plugin reads no environment variable at all, unless the provider also sets its `_shellenv` field (typed in the plugin, not documented there): that variable is then read first and the command second. So a provider switched to `cmd:` without it would stop working from a shell that ran your loader.
20: - Our own provider resolver treats a `cmd:` name as "needs no key", so the first provider in our preference list with one is chosen without a check, and the fallback to the next provider would never happen. That is ours to settle in the change; it is not something the dotfiles need to do.
21: 
22: ## What Neovim needs from the dotfiles
23: 
24: Nothing. The key store stays the dotfiles' decision; our configuration will never hold a key value (decision D21 of our roadmap).
25: If the user takes the item, I will tell you the route he chose, so the per-tool tracking can point at the change.

109: - Names of secret variables: only publicly well-known ones (a provider's documented convention), never a name specific to this workstation; the private repository's name never in a committed file; neutral alias `private_store` for its directory.
110: - Orchestration state lives in `.state/` of the checkout, not `/tmp/opencode`.
111: - Close a finished agent's tab (and worktree) once its session is exported; the orchestrator does it.
112: - History of this repository accepted as it is; real name and address stay for new commits for now.
113: - Commit messages are proposed first and committed only after the user says "commit"; push only on "push".
114: - An agent never prints the environment, `chezmoi data`, `chezmoi dump-config`, `systemctl --user show-environment` or an unfiltered herdr listing; facts about keys come as counts or booleans, computed in memory.
115: - A permission prompt in another agent's pane is read (`herdr pane read`), reported to the user and left to him: never answered by me.
116: 
117: ## Habits that bit me, again
118: 
119: - zsh: `set -- $var` and `$var` holding several words do not split; `echo ==` is equals-expansion; an unmatched glob aborts the command; `2>&1 >/dev/null | next` also pipes stdout; `mapfile` is bash-only.
120: - Tool calls sent in the same batch run in parallel: a `chmod` and the command it fixes must share a shell line (TokenScope ran before the `chmod`).
121: - Plan mode blocks `herdr agent prompt` to another agent: draft the message, wait for build mode.
122: - `rtk` condenses or hides output (`rtk ls` hid files): use `/usr/bin/grep -a`, plain `rg`, `/usr/bin/ls` for anything that decides something.
123: - A scan helper that prints zero added lines, or a `wc` on a directory, is a bug until the count is shown beside it: verify by listing (I wrongly read a spec directory as empty).
124: - `umask` prints `0002` in bash and `002` in zsh: normalise before comparing; reading `/proc/<pid>/environ` of other users prints errors: wrap the loop body in `{ ...; } 2>/dev/null`.
125: - A fleet agent can exit after its last message (`nvim-s26`): check `herdr agent list` before relying on a name.
126: - `scm:worktree:done` refuses on an untracked file (an editor's grammar server writes `.spell/`): check no process uses it, delete that directory only.
127: - `git commit | head` kills git on SIGPIPE in the hook.

Your two points check out as follows. The current recipe does clean up, but it doesn't group the worktree the way herdr does.

## What the recipe does today
- **Grouping:** no. `scm:worktree:new --tab --workspace wN` creates the git worktree, then a plain tab inside `wN`. herdr has its own model, a primary workspace with its "linked worktree workspaces", which `herdr workspace close --group` closes together. Our tab doesn't use it: `herdr worktree list` would show the builder's worktree with no workspace of its own (`open_workspace_id` empty).
- **Cleanup:** yes, but the order isn't enforced.
  - `scm:worktree:done` checks the merge into `origin/main`, then hands over to `rm`.
  - `rm` refuses a dirty or unmerged worktree and runs the project's hook. It then removes the mise trust, the git worktree and the local branch, and closes the tab unless `--keep-tab` is given.
  - Nothing in these tasks requires the export first. That ordering is my procedure: export, commit, push, then close by id and `done --keep-tab`. That part is only in the "Procedures" section of the resume note, not in the launch recipe.

## Plan (build mode)
1. **Launch with grouping:**
   - `scm:worktree:new` without `--tab`. It keeps the duplicate checks, the mise trust, the project hook and the start-commit file that `done` needs.
   - Then `herdr worktree open --workspace wN --path <worktree> --label env-build --no-focus`, which opens the worktree as a linked workspace grouped under `wN`.
   - I read the new workspace's id and root pane from the JSON, start the agent there (`herdr agent start chezmoi-env-builder --kind opencode --pane <pane> -- --agent build --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`), check the status line and send the prompt.
2. **Cleanup in the recipe:**
   1. Export the builder's session, commit and push it.
   2. `herdr workspace close <linked workspace id>`, never with `--group`, which would also close `wN` and this pane.
   3. `mise run scm:worktree:done feat/correct-shell-environment`, which removes the worktree, the branch and the prune entry.
   4. Check that `herdr worktree list --workspace wN` shows only `main`, then add the journal lines.
3. **Documents:**
   - Rewrite the recipe in `.state/resume.md` (launch and cleanup), and the reporting fallback in `builder-brief.md`. The builder will no longer sit in a tab of `wN`. The fallback becomes: find the primary workspace of the group, then its `orch` tab.
   - Propose an edit to the Workflow paragraph of `AGENTS.md`, which today says "tab closed by id … `--keep-tab`". That one needs a commit, so I'll propose the message.
4. **Still to verify when it runs:** I can't test these in plan mode, because those commands write.
   - Whether `worktree open` accepts a worktree created by git.
   - Which fields its JSON returns.
   - Whether it asks for herdr's repository trust.
   - That closing a linked workspace without `--group` is accepted.

**Output:**
```
- `tmp/`: scratch of the checkout, mode 0700, for what a session needs and does not keep.
  Raw session exports are the exception: they stay in a scratch directory outside the repository until they are redacted and deleted.
- `journal.md`: append-only log, one line per event (briefs written, prompts sent, worktrees created and removed, merges, pushes): `- YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS <actor> <event>`.
- `git worktree remove` deletes the ignored files of a worktree with it: a brief that must last is copied into its change folder, and nothing else lives only in a worktree's `.state/`.
- Ignored files are not scanned by the commit hook, so a brief or a journal never holds a secret value.

An agent that works a change (a lead, a builder, a closer) is finished when its work is merged or handed over and its session is exported.
Then its tab is closed by id (`herdr tab close <id>`) and, when it had a worktree, the worktree goes with `scm:worktree:done <branch> --keep-tab`; the orchestrator does both, after the export is committed.
A finished agent is not left open in a tab: it holds a context nobody uses, and a stale pane has been mistaken for a live one.

<!-- vim: set ts=2 sts=2 sw=2 et endofline fixendofline spell spl=en : -->
--- last log entries of the observations (headings of the launches)
--- proposal: What Changes section end and Impact
## What Changes

- **Model.**
  A branch has one read-write checkout at a time (git enforces it), so a branch implies a path.
  A herdr workspace is built out of a worktree and is the home of the agents and sessions that work in it.
  Coordination across the project (orchestration, synchronization, messages between workspaces) stays one level up, in the workspace of the main checkout.
  Whether a workspace should also carry its own orchestration is not decided here.
- **Shared Python library** in the global mise lib directory, standard library only, ported from the Neovim repository's delivery module and its herdr wrapper, replacing `scm_prompt_agent`:
  - bounded herdr calls (a timeout on each, `timeout` as an error code);
  - the first prompt is delivered once: wait for idle, wait for the TUI to draw, submit with `--wait --until working`, inspect before any retry (`working` or `done` means delivered, `blocked` stops, the prompt 
  - lookups of the state of a branch, a worktree, a workspace and an agent name.
- **Two new global tasks** (names to confirm in the design):
  - `workspace:open <branch|path>` creates, or reuses, the herdr workspace of a worktree, and prints one JSON line.
  - `agent:launch <branch>` does the whole flow: creates the worktree when the branch is new (through `scm:worktree:new`), opens its workspace, starts the agent (default kind OpenCode, plan mode by default, opt
- **Checks before anything is created.**
  Each case ends in reuse, create or refuse, and a refusal names what it found:

  - the branch exists, is checked out, and where;
  - a workspace is already open on that path (reuse);
  - a workspace has the requested label but another path, or several share the label (refuse);
  - the agent name is taken (refuse).
- **`agent:dispatch` and `scm:worktree:new --prompt`** keep their interfaces and use the library; both print one JSON line with the delivery outcome.
  `scm:worktree:new --tab` resolves `--workspace` before it creates anything and names the value it was given.
  The help of `--prompt` warns that a text ending in `@file` may swallow the Enter.
- **Tests.**
  Python unit tests with a fake `herdr` that counts how many times the text reached the input box (`tests/global-mise-tasks/`, at the repository root and so outside the source state: no ignore entry), plus a li
- **Replaces `fix-prompt-delivery`.**
  Every requirement of that change moves into the `agent-launch` capability, its directory is deleted (it holds planning only; git keeps the history), and its audit row is marked as superseded.
  Its closing duty moves here: when this change is applied, the Neovim repository is told, so that `session:start` can use the global tasks.
- **Depends on `add-repo-roadmap`** for the amended rule on Python in the global tasks directory (shell files pass `shellcheck -x`, Python files compile and have unit tests).
- **Observations.**
  The launch of the roadmap agent, done by hand with the model above, is logged in `observations.md` in this folder: it is the input for the design and for a signal to the fleet's study of multi-agent orchestra
- **Non-goals.**
  - The architecture of multi-agent orchestration, and where a launcher belongs in the fleet's tooling (this repository or the fleet's tools).
    The tasks stay small so that they can move.
  - Any edit to the Neovim repository: it gets a signal to adopt the tasks, after this change is applied.
  - Choosing the agent's model: only passing settings through.



```
